Achievements: Achievements are goals you can earn across your campaigns: a first harvest, a castle taken by terms, a century without a broken oath, Constantinople held past 1460, Moscow free of the khan after Kulikovo. There are 80 at launch, the same list on Steam, Game Center and Google Play Games. They are earned only in ironman campaigns, and they never give anything inside the game: no bonus, no unlocked nation, no cosmetic. How it works Fair and our own - One list everywhere. Steam, Game Center and Google Play Games share the same achievements. - Our own goals. Every achievement is written for Pocket Hegemony's own systems; no name, condition or icon is taken from another commercial game. - Situations, not countries. A test describes a situation. Where a historical event is involved, it uses the event's role, so whoever holds that role can earn it. Only One Island Realm and Lord of the River Bend name a region. - Nothing for harm. No achievement is tied to a narrative-only event, to conquering a named people, or to sacking or scorching land. - Grounded. Every test reads a stat or a moment that an existing design defines; where the system is not designed yet, the row points at the gap list. - No luck-only goals. Each goal can be planned for. Tiers and points Tier Points Meant for At launch Copper 5 One action, or a goal most players reach in their first campaign 40 Silver 10 A goal you aim for 25 Gold 20 A whole campaign shaped around it 12 Crown 40 The hardest 3 Points show on Game Center and Google Play, not Steam. The list holds at most 100 achievements, ever, counting retired ones. Every achievement's points are a multiple of 5 and at most 40, and the total is at most 1,000. Launch ships 80 achievements worth 810 points, keeping 20 slots and 190 points for updates; after any update at least 10 slots and 100 points stay in reserve, and spare points should go mostly to new copper and silver goals. If a score or victory is added to the game, it gets its own achievements from the reserve. Names are at most 24 characters and texts at most 100. These limits are the strictest of the three stores: Limit Steam Game Center Google Play Games Adopted Number 100 until Valve's confidence check 100 200 to 400 100 at most, ever Points none max 100 each, 1,000 total multiples of 5, 5 to 200 each, 1,000 total (newer docs 2,000) multiples of 5, max 40, 1,000 total Hidden yes yes yes yes, spoilers only Progress stats at set steps percent incremental, up to 10,000 steps one game counter, reported each store's way Icon 64 × 64 512 or 1024 512 32 × 32 pixel art, scaled by whole numbers Scope and hidden achievements Most achievements are campaign scope: the whole condition must be met inside one game. Seven are lifetime : their counter adds up across games in your player profile and is mirrored to the store's progress where it has one. There is no hidden achievement at launch; hidden is kept for later event chains whose very existence is the surprise. A hidden achievement shows as "Hidden achievement" with its tier, its name and text secret until earned. Some achievements are levels of a ladder : one count at rising steps. The harvest ladder counts province harvests (each of your provinces that brings in its harvest adds one) across all your campaigns: First Harvest at 1, then Ten Harvests , A Hundred Harvests , A Thousand Harvests and Ten Thousand Harvests . Each level is its own achievement with its own points, as the stores have no levels, but the game shows the ladder as one badge marked with the level reached, such as 3/5. When tests run Each achievement names a moment , and when that moment occurs only the tests of rows naming it run. A date row is checked once, on that day, and never for a day on or before the day your campaign started. Tests run after the turn's own systems, at the very end of the turn order, so they read final values. If the test does not hold when its moment comes, the achievement stays locked. The moments are: turn end, year end, harvest, spring start, a date, battle end, sea battle end, siege end, war end, rebellion end, relation changed, province gained, invention done, regiment trained, lord created, charter granted, loan closed, style adopted, colony founded, contact made, fleet home, food policy changed, event choice, event end, 12 months after a succession, and campaign end. Which games count A campaign earns achievements only while all three hold: Save flag Must be ironman unbroken true: the campaign started as ironman and never left it cheat marked false: no debug, editor or "free play" cheat was used, even once switched country false: you still play the realm you started with A campaign that is not ironman earns nothing, for good. A cheat marks the save for good, and nothing from it is awarded, in-game or on any store. Playing on as another country after game over stops achievements from that moment. Any difficulty counts, with historical or free events. The tutorial earns none, and its last card tells you achievements start in a real campaign. Lifetime counters only count campaigns that pass all three flags. The pause menu and the new game screen show whether the campaign can earn achievements, and you are warned once before an action that would end eligibility (turning on a cheat, switching country after game over). Progress bars 18 rows have a progress bar: a game counter reported to each store against its target. Store How progress is reported Google Play An incremental achievement; targets above 10,000 are reported in steps (people in tens of thousands, gold in tens) Game Center Percent complete Steam A stat bound to the achievement, with a progress popup at 25, 50 and 75 percent Campaign counters reset with each new game, and progress goes to a store only when it beats the best value already reported there, so a store's progress never goes down. The in-game list shows this campaign's own value. Offline and failed calls An unlock is written to your profile and shown in-game at once, whether or not a store is reachable. Unlocks that have not reached a store wait in a queue, sent whenever the store is reachable and retried at start-up and every few minutes. On start-up the game reads the store's list and sends anything it is missing, so a new phone or a reinstall catches up. Free tier and Steam demo The free iOS and Android download awards achievements as the full game does, and you keep them when you buy. A row marked full game cannot be earned with the free tier's countries alone; the free countries are the Ottomans and France, so at launch these are Our Own Banner , Free of the Khan , Blackbird Field , The Walls Held , The Conqueror's Heirs , The Four Quarters Hold , From One Hall , Many Tents, One People , Many Crowns and Crowns of the World . The Steam demo awards nothing to Steam directly; it keeps a local list from its ironman games, and when you buy the full game it reads the demo's profile and awards what you earned there. Store ids and retiring An achievement's id is never renamed after release, and every store id comes from it: Steam uses ACH plus the id in capitals; Game Center uses the bundle id plus .ach. plus the id; Google Play's console-generated ids are kept in achievements.google.json . A build step writes each store's upload file (Steam's VDF or web form, App Store Connect's list, Google's CSV) from the YAML, with localised names and texts. A retired achievement is hidden in every store and its test turned off, but never deleted, so you keep what you earned. Icons Each achievement has one 32 × 32 icon in the game's pixel-art palette, with a 2-pixel frame in its tier's colour (copper, silver, gold, crown purple-gold). Icons are scaled with nearest-neighbour and no smoothing: × 2 for Steam (64) and × 16 for Game Center and Google Play (512). Steam's locked image uses the grey "unknown land" parchment tones of the map's fog. Each icon shows what the achievement is about, never a real flag or coat of arms. the icon, name and tier, and a short chip-tune sting. Selecting one shows its text, progress and the date earned. An "earnable in this campaign" filter shows achievements not yet earned and not already ruled out (for example a date that has passed). - The turn report gets one line per unlock, with a jump to where it happened when there is a place (the castle, the battlefield). - Eligibility shows on the pause menu and the new game screen, with a one-time warning before you lose it. In the playable build today - Open the game menu (the three-line button at the top left) and tap Achievements , or Achievements on the start screen. The Achievements card opens in the side panel: earned of 80 and points of 810 at the top, the eligibility line, a filter ( All , Within reach , Earned ), then one row of badges per category with its own count. Tap a badge for its text, tier and points, this campaign's progress bar, and the date you earned it. The harvest ladder is one badge in First steps with its level in the corner (3/5); its detail lists every level with its target and date and a bar to the next level, counted across all your campaigns. - A badge is the tier's frame round the category's sign (a coin for Realm, swords for War, an anchor for Sea…) until the icons are drawn. Grey means locked; a dashed frame means Not in the game yet : 23 rows read systems the build does not have yet (charters, rulers and succession, trade hubs, winter quarters, marshals, styles, voyages and colonies, rebellions, regions of the world), and they stay locked until those land. The four History rows of the decades after 1378 read the bridge events (Kulikovo, Kosovo, Ankara, Timur's death); they can be earned once those events run in your campaign. - When you earn one, a banner slides in under the date bar for three seconds and a line goes into the News; tap the banner to open the card at it. The game menu button (and the Achievements line in it) carries a red dot until you have looked. Achievement toasts in Settings → Gameplay turns the banner off; achievements still unlock. - Tests run at the end of each week's turn, after everything else. What you earn is kept on this device, apart from any campaign, so it stays when you start again or reload. The build has no saves yet, so every campaign counts as ironman. Buildings: Buildings are how your provinces put people to work. Every farm, mine, loom house, church, castle and harbour stands on a tile, a town slot or across the whole province, gives job slots to one class of people, makes something, and costs gold, materials, labourers and months to build and gold every month to keep. This page covers where buildings can go, what they cost, how sites run, upgrades and conversions, upkeep and condition, who owns them, what the people build for themselves, the full catalogue with its landmarks, and the screens for managing it all. How it works What a building is Every building has: Field Meaning Type Farm, loom house, castle … Place The tile, town slot or ring-works position it stands on Step How far it has been upgraded: 1 to 3, castles and a few others more Owner Crown, lord, clergy, town, merchant house or company, or the people Jobs Slots for one class , and how many are filled. Filled slots make wares; empty ones make nothing Makes What it produces Needs Wares it eats, and anything that must be nearby Condition Sound, neglected, damaged or ruined Upkeep Gold the owner pays every month, shown as a yearly total A building has at most one effect besides its jobs and wares, and never gives a flat percentage to a whole country. Where buildings go - Land tiles (fields, pasture, woods, marsh, waste) each hold one land building that fits the tile's use. - Shore tiles each hold one shore building: fishery, saltworks, harbour, shipyard, bridge, lighthouse or naval base. - The castle tile holds the province's one castle. Its granary is part of the castle, not a second building. - Town slots , by town size: Town size Hamlet Village Market town Town City Great city Town slots 1 2 4 6 9 12 The capital gets one extra slot, held for the palace. Town walls and landmarks outside the town (a monastery, an observatory) don't use a slot. - Ring works belong to the whole province and take no tile or slot: road, canal, town walls, wells and drains, dykes and watchtower line. One of each per province, with steps. If a town shrinks below its building count, the buildings stay but the extra ones are neglected until the town grows back. You choose which on a prompt; the AI drops the newest. Limits: Limit Buildings One per province Market, seat, school, mint, drill yard, arsenal, hospital, bank, harbour, shipyard, lighthouse, rail station, power station One per faith per town House of worship One per realm, in the capital Palace, chancery, diet hall, hostage residence, parliament house As many as there are places Ware-making buildings: farms, ranches, mines, loom houses, forges and the rest What a building costs Every building and every step costs gold, materials, labourers and months . - The owner pays the gold up front when the site starts, from their own treasury (the crown's, a lord's wealth, the clergy's or the town's). - Gold and months , but not materials, are multiplied by the ground: farmland ×1, hills ×1.25, mountains ×2, jungle ×2. - Cancelling refunds half the gold and the materials not yet used. Materials (timber, stone, bricks, earth, iron, steel, concrete) come from the province's own wares first, then from any of your provinces in reach (the province itself, one ring away, or further along roads and rivers), then are bought at the province's price: Material Bought for (gold a load) Notes Timber 0.5 Stone 0.5 Double price more than 3 provinces from any quarry Bricks 0.8 Count as stone, one for one Earth free, made on site Instead of stone in drylands, desert or savanna, but the building's upkeep doubles Iron 2 From era IV Steel 3 From era VI Concrete 3 From era VI Bought materials are dearer in a province with few traders. Labourers. Every site needs a crew (for example 500 for a farm, 3,000 for a stone castle, 6,000 for a canal). The crew comes from the province's homeless first ; while they work they are fed, steal nothing and don't count toward homeless trouble. If there aren't enough homeless, the rest come from every class by share, leaving their slots empty while they build. With half a crew the site takes twice the months; with none it stops. When the site is done, homeless crew who fit the new building's class move into its slots, the rest go back to being homeless, and other classes return to their slots. Sites - One site per place at a time. - The crown runs two sites per province at once: one on the land, one in the town. - A master of works official adds one more land and one more town site and halves the months. - Lords run their own sites in their own provinces with their own gold, without using the crown's. - Sites on the land stop in the coldest month of a cold climate and the wettest month of a monsoon climate. - Every site stops while an enemy army is in the province. While the province is occupied, sites stop and the occupier can loot their materials. A sacked town loses its town site. Buildings can also be gained by a lord, the clergy, a town or the people building them, by conquest (with their owners if they stay), by an event, or from the start of the game. Steps and upgrades Each step has its own gold, materials and months. While a building is being upgraded it keeps working at its old step, except a castle, whose walls count one step lower during the work. An upgrade isn't allowed until its needs are met (an invention, a town size, a nearby building, a charter). A building drops one step after 10 years of neglect, when sacked, or when hit by an earthquake. A step-1 building that falls becomes ruined. The market shows how steps work: weekly market (1,500 market folk, village or bigger), yearly fair (2,400, needs T6 Merchant fairs , a market charter and a market town; fairs standing at the start stay), trading house (3,000, needs T3 Bills of exchange and a town or bigger). Upkeep and condition Upkeep is paid every month by the owner, a twelfth of the yearly figure: Group Yearly upkeep Farms, ranches, fisheries, lumber camps 0 to 0.5 gold Mines, quarries, craft buildings, markets 0.5 to 2 Schools, hospitals, almshouses 2 to 6 Castles 3 (earthwork) to 20 (star fort), more with a garrison Landmarks and the palace 5 to 30 The clergy pay for houses of worship unless the crown takes it over. Your total building upkeep shows on the Treasury card's Upkeep line. Condition: Condition How it gets there Works Way back Sound Fully Neglected Upkeep unpaid in a month, or the town shrinks below it At half Upkeep paid again for a full season (3 months) Damaged Fire, flood, earthquake, a siege breach (castle), a bad raid At half, and nothing in its first season Repair at half gold, half materials, half months Ruined Its tile burned, a town building plundered, a castle razed, a step-1 building after 10 years of neglect Not at all Rebuild at half cost, or clear it for something else In peace, burned (ruined) land buildings rebuild by themselves, one a year; town buildings need an owner to pay. How buildings are lost or damaged - Foraging or looting armies burn land buildings tile by tile. - A raid damages one building, or ruins it if the raid is big. Town walls stop raids reaching town buildings. - A plundered town loses 1 in 3 of its town buildings, or 1 in 6 with town walls. - Rebels holding a province loot one town building a season, the market first. - A town fire is rolled each year in timber towns, more likely in big towns and shanty camps and less where most buildings are stone or brick; it damages one to three town buildings. - A flood in a river or marsh province damages land buildings on shore and marsh tiles; a dyke broken in war turns fields to marsh. - An earthquake event in a quake region damages one building in three and takes castles a step down. - Demolishing returns a quarter of the materials and overflows the workers. A peace treaty can demand named castles be demolished. - A tile changing use (woods cleared, the town growing over fields) ends the building that no longer fits. A mine closes when its ore deposit runs out. Converting - A farm changes its crop (grain, flax, cotton, dyes) in one season at no cost. While it grows anything but grain it feeds nobody, and the province card warns you if that would leave the province short. - A house of worship can be given to another faith, when and at the cost in grievances Religion sets. - A craft building can change its trade, and a factory its product, at half the cost of building the new one. - Slighting pulls a castle down to a ruin (so no rebel or rival can use it), which rebuilds at half cost. Owners The owner pays upkeep and decides upgrades, demolition and conversion. Owner What they build and own Crown Anything. If the crown pays for a building in a lord's province, the lord owns it and his loyalty rises one step Lord By trait: Builder the most; Greedy markets and mines; Pious houses of worship and monasteries; Warlike castles and drill yards; by his wealth and what his provinces lack. His buildings go with him if he defects, and come to the crown if his line dies out or his land is seized Clergy Houses of worship (one in every town of their faith first), then monasteries, almshouses where there are homeless, hospitals in plague years, and church schools, by the faith's share Town (with a Town law charter) Market steps, walls, a bridge, then guild halls and craft buildings, by traders and wealth. The crown can't demolish or seize them without breaking the charter Merchant house or company (Mining right or company charter, T8 and T9) Mines, warehouses, trading houses, plantations and overseas posts, by trade value; keeps half their output The people (commons) Basic land buildings, with no upkeep. Demolishing one gives the province Burned homes What the people build themselves - Village works : at the end of each year, in a province at peace for 5 years with more than 3 months of food in store and homeless people or full slots, there is a 20 % chance the people put up a step-1 farm, ranch, fishery or lumber camp on an empty matching tile, owned by the commons. - Craft buildings appearing : now and then a loom house, tannery, kiln or brewery appears in a town with a market, homeless people and the raw ware nearby, owned by the town or the commons. See Research. Landmarks A landmark is a real, named building that stood or was built between 1378 and 1939. It counts as a step above its building type and has one effect of its own, written as a count. Landmarks are never on the build sheet: they are on the map at the start or founded by an event when the historical requirements are met. An event may found one elsewhere or not at all, but there are no invented landmarks. Landmark Place At the start? Regional looks and unique variants A building has the same effect everywhere ; only its name and sprite change with the province's region and faith (a caravanserai is a khan, funduq or tambo; a palace a kremlin or saray). Separately, six unique variants (Külliye, Kontor, Qollqa line, Polder mill, Ever-normal granary, Funduq quarter) are offered to National Strengths, each changing one number or adding one line; that system decides whether to use them. Events Events change buildings with five effects: add a building (placed on a fitting empty tile or slot, or if none, the province's least-filled building goes up a step), remove one (it is ruined), damage a share of the province's buildings, move a building a step up or down, and the condition "has this building at this step". The old province stats map too: prosperity +2 gives two fitting buildings, fort level +1 a castle step, infrastructure +1 a road step, industry +1 a factory. Starting buildings - Buildings follow the map's wealth: wealth 1 has a farm or ranch on a third of its tiles; wealth 10 has every tile built and town buildings at step 2. - Town size follows population, and town slots fill by a regional template. - Houses of worship's faith, lords' buildings and landmarks come from the catalogue; allowed buildings and steps from start inventions. - Harbours and shipyards come from the start's port list. - Fixed mines, named markets and landmarks come from event anchors: Potosí (from 1545 by event), Kutná Hora, Falun; Bruges, the Champagne fairs, Malacca. See The 1378 Start. The AI The AI builds by the same rules and costs. Each month each AI country looks at one province in turn and picks at most one building there, by the first rule that fits: 1. Repair a ruined or damaged building, if it can pay. 2. A hungry province (Hungry, or under 3 months of food): a food building on an empty tile, or a granary at the nearest castle. 3. Homeless over 5 %: the building whose class takes most of them. 4. A raw ware going unused: its craft building. 5. A frontier province of a country expecting war: a castle step or walls. 6. Faith or trade gaps: a house of worship where its faith is low; a market or caravanserai on a busy path. 7. Its personality: mercantile builds markets and harbours, isolationist schools, hegemon seeker castles and drill yards. It keeps a year's upkeep in reserve and never starts a site it can't crew. On a phone this is about 400 small checks a month in a 400-country world. Each month A turn is one week. These steps run once a month, in the turn in which a new month begins. Cadence What happens Monthly Upkeep paid or unpaid; sites advance; finished buildings open their job slots before overflow runs; the AI checks one province Each season Farms, groves and fisheries make food; a damaged building's first-season penalty ends; rebels loot Yearly Wares made; neglect years counted; village works and craft buildings appearing; town fire roll; burned land buildings rebuild one a year in peace; Works advice worked out Each building stores just five small numbers (type, step, owner, condition, filled jobs); sites live in one realm-level list. Worked example: Troyes, 1444 to 1452 (on the 1444 checkpoint world) Troyes starts with 12 tiles (4 farms, a burned field, 2 ranches, a lumber camp, an empty woods tile, a fishery on the Seine, the castle and the town), 3,600 homeless, and a town with 6 full slots: a market, 3 loom houses, a church and a school. 1. 1444, the burned field. You pay 15 gold, half the cost of a farm, to rebuild it in a season instead of waiting a year. 500 homeless form the crew and then move into the farm's slots. 2. 1445, the yearly fair. No free slot, so you upgrade the market to a yearly fair (France has learned T6 and a market charter is granted; 100 gold, 30 stone, 12 months). Troyes has no quarry; the stone comes free from one in the hills one ring away, in a lord's province, which counts as the crown's own. The crew of 2,000 is all homeless. The fair takes 900 more market folk, and traders can now be hired here. 3. 1447, the town grows to a city with 9 slots: a drill yard (40 gold), a warehouse (30 gold) and a fourth loom house (35 gold). Each crew takes the homeless first, leaving 400, under 1 %, and no theft. 4. 1449, the woods tile. You want a farm, but clearing the woods would leave the lumber camp as the only timber, and the shipyard downriver needs it. You leave the woods and build a quarry on a hills tile of a neighbouring province for 20 gold, so the next castle step needs no bought stone. 5. 1450, Burgundy invades. The stone castle upgrade site stops; foragers burn 2 fields; the town is besieged and takes honours of war. With only a palisade, plunder would have burned 1 in 3 town buildings; because the town took terms, none burn. 6. 1452, peace. Troyes has 2 ruined farms rebuilding by themselves, one a year, its fair intact and a castle site to restart. Its upkeep is 7 gold a year against 13 gold of tax reaching the crown. In the game now: works, the first cut Until jobs, wares and labourers are in the game, you build ten works for the crown. Each costs gold, paid when its site opens, and months to raise: Work Where What it does now Farm (mill farm, enclosed farm) fields tiles works every fields tile: its farmers feed 1.1, 1.3 or 1.5 people a step, against 0.67 on bare land Ranch pasture tiles works every pasture tile: herders feed 1.33 against 0.67; wool Fishery shore tiles works every shore tile: seafolk feed 1.33 against 0.67 Lumber camp woods tiles timber: works needing it here cost 20 % less; its timber is traded Quarry rocky waste tiles stone: works needing it here cost 20 % less; its stone is traded Market (weekly market, yearly fair, trading house) a village or bigger trade value +25 %, +50 %, +100 % by step; 4, 8, 16 trader visits a month at full value; traders are founded here (Trade) Harbour (port, great port) a coast ships stop and trade here; trade value +25 % to ships Drill yard (barracks) a town recruits +15 % a step Road (track, road) anywhere armies march 15 % faster a step, and traders with them Castle (earthwork ring fort, stone castle) anywhere walls: armies must besiege it Slots. Every province has slots by its people: 2, and one more at 10,000, 30,000, 100,000, 300,000 and 1,000,000 people (so 2 to 7). Every work takes one slot, whatever it is, and keeps it as it grows a step. The same steps give the town its size, from hamlet to great city, which some steps need (a market needs a village). The Build tab's first line says how many slots are taken. The farm, ranch and fishery work the province's land, which is laid out in tiles (see Provinces, In the game now: the land ): the building stands in the province and takes one slot, and each tile of its use holds work for its people. The other effects are stand-ins, written into the rules ( defines.works ) until the jobs and wares model replaces them. A step needs its invention: the stone castle needs Stone castles, the road needs Roads and post stations. How you use it. Tap a province, then its Build tab. At the top are its sites with the months left, and its queue, where ▲ and ▼ move a build and Drop takes it off (nothing was paid). Below is the build sheet: every work the land suits, at its next step, with what it does, its gold, months and upkeep. Tap Build . When the site is busy or the gold isn't there yet, the button says Queue and the build waits its turn. Stop on a running site gives half its gold back. A province raises one work on its land and one in its town at a time. The overview. A province's Build tab shows its sites, its queue and what stands there; the country card has no Works tab. On the map, a striking hammer marks each of your sites. A finished work is announced over the map with Go there . Upkeep. Works cost upkeep each month, as the Works line of the treasury ledger. In a month the treasury is empty, your works give only half. At the start the map's castles and forts stand, every capital has a stone castle, and richer provinces start with farms, ranches, markets, harbours and tracks. Other realms build too. Each month every realm at peace looks at one of its provinces and orders the first of a market, a farm, a harbour, a road, walls on a border or a drill yard that fits there, if it keeps a year of upkeep in hand. What you see The building card , when you tap a building on the tile row: Every field opens its gain and lose list. The build sheet , when you tap an empty tile, an empty town slot or Build on the province card: Costs and months are already multiplied by the ground. A grey row says what is missing ( needs Water and wind mills , needs a town of 6 slots ). The Works screen , one screen for the whole realm, opened from the country card: - Advice : at most five suggestions, worked out once a year from empty tiles, homeless people and wares that arrive unused. - Build all advised queues every suggestion that fits the gold you set aside. - Batch orders build one thing everywhere it fits, such as a granary at every castle. On the map : at world zoom only landmarks (a small icon); at region zoom the castle, town size, harbour anchor, a hammer on provinces with a site, and a cracked icon for neglected or damaged buildings; at local zoom each building's sprite and step, with scaffolding and ash. The Works map mode colours sites green, neglected or damaged amber and ruined red; the Jobs map mode shows empty job slots against homeless people. See Map and Map Modes. Turn report : one line per finished building, one per building lost, and one in the month upkeep first goes unpaid. Culture: Culture in Pocket Hegemony is about language : the people a person belongs to, the speech they share and the land they see as their own. Every person has a language, every country has one court language, and everyone in your realm is of the same language, related, foreign or a trading people to that court. Each year languages slowly drift, and you steer that drift with your Language policy, your schools and your officials. How it works Languages and families Every person has a language, and every language belongs to exactly one family. There are only these two levels, family and language, with no sub-languages. The game has about 600 languages in 43 families. The families are the event tree's 39 culture groups plus four added ones: celtic, baltic, caucasian and hebrew. Language Family French latin Occitan latin Breton celtic Mandinka mande Swahili bantu Lithuanian baltic Georgian, Armenian caucasian Jewish hebrew Criollo creole atlantic The world's catalogue has 1,468 culture strings. They are mapped onto languages once, folding only near-duplicates (so "Jews" and "Jewish communities" both become Jewish, "Swabians" become High German and "Westphalians" Low German). The original string stays as the language's local name in tooltips, and any string that can't be mapped goes on a review list. Languages are kept apart where history turns on the split: French and Occitan, Castilian and Catalan, Great Russian and Ruthenian, High German and Low German. Regional peoples stay separate until a nation-building event merges them. Each language has an id, a name, a family, a homeland (the provinces it sees as its own), a way of life (settled, herding, forest, seafaring or trading) and a diaspora flag. Some also have a language they merge into or split into. For example, Castilian is a settled latin language that splits to Criollo, Dyula is a trading diaspora, and Tuscan merges into Italian. There is no culture meter, no "cultural power" and no list of accepted cultures. What matters is simply who your people are and how they relate to your court. The court language Every country has one court language: the language of the ruler's house and court. At the start it is the first culture in the country's catalogue record, so France starts with French. When a dynasty of another language takes the throne, by conquest, inheritance, marriage or a lord's revolt, the court language becomes that dynasty's language. If a French dynasty took England, French would become England's court language and French people would share England's court language. The game then works out again who is kin and which lords share the court language, and the music palette changes from the next track. Same language, related, foreign and trading peoples Everyone in your realm has one relation to your court: Relation Who Counts toward Language % Dot Same language People of your court language 1 green Related Another language of the same family 0.5 yellow Foreign A language of another family 0 red Trading people A diaspora language 0 grey For France, French people share the court language, Occitans are related, and Bretons and Flemings are foreign. Language % on your country card is the share of the realm's people of the same language, plus half of those of a related one. It is worked out whenever you open the card and is never stored. Worked example. France holds 6.9 million French, 1.6 million Occitan, 0.5 million Breton, 0.4 million Flemish, 0.1 million Basque and 0.02 million Jewish people. That is 6.9 of the same language plus half of 1.6 related, so 7.7 out of 9.52 million, and the Language % is 81. A trading people is never foreign when grievances are worked out: a Jewish community in Paris gives no Foreign rule . They don't count toward Language % either. Before nationalism rises, Foreign rule only comes from homelands of foreign languages, never from related ones. While nationalism in a province is under 0.3, French-ruled Brittany has Foreign rule but Toulouse, the Occitan homeland, does not. Drift Once a year, after births and deaths, people in every province drift a little toward one language: the court's, or the local majority's. Which language pulls. The court language pulls if the province has been held 20 years or more and is governed by any of your officials (whatever his own language) or by a lord of the court language. Otherwise the province's majority language pulls. Rennes (mostly Breton) held Governed by Drifts toward 20 years a royal official French 25 years a French lord French 25 years a Breton lord Breton 19 years a royal official Breton So in a province held only 5 years, like Kent with its English majority, a Norman minority melts into English. How fast. People who already speak that language don't move. Everyone else moves toward it at a base rate of 0.5 % a year, times every multiplier that applies: Condition Multiplier Town classes (craftsmen, market folk, clerks, scholars) × 2 Related to the language it drifts toward × 2 A school teaching in the language it drifts toward × 1.5 A Schoolmaster official serving in the province × 2 Language policy Let be / Teach / Impose × 0.5 / × 1 / × 2 The province is the drifting language's homeland × 0.5 A herding, forest or seafaring language in its own kind of land (see below) × 0.5 A trading people × 0.25 The province's nationalism is 0.3 or more × 0.25 Each of printing, mass schooling, newspapers and railways × 1.25 An Own language charter (drift toward the court language) stops it A school of another language counts for that language instead. A school teaching a learned language, Latin or Classical Arabic, speeds no one's drift, because nobody grows up speaking it. Own kind of land. Herding peoples are at home on grassland and drylands (the steppe), forest peoples in forest and jungle, and seafaring peoples in any province on the sea. There they drift at half speed. So if France has printing and railways, Flemish farmers drift at 0.5 % × 1.25 × 1.25, which is 1.5625 times the base. Worked example: Troyes. France has the court language French and the policy Teach. Troyes is 94 % French and 6 % Flemish, has been French for 200 years, is run by a royal official, and has a school teaching in French. At the end of the year French pulls. The Flemish drift at 0.5 % × 1.5 for the school × 1 for Teach = 0.75 %, about 32 people. No French people move. If a Schoolmaster also served there, the rate would double to 1.5 %. Small and new languages. A province holds at most three languages. A language that falls below 1 % is removed (if Troyes ends a year with 0.9 % Flemish, Flemish is gone). When a fourth language arrives, it gets in only if it is larger than the smallest of the three; whichever group is smallest then joins the majority. If Riga is Latvian 60 %, German 30 % and Russian 10 % and Swedes as many as 15 % of Riga arrive, Swedish replaces Russian and the Russians join the Latvians. If only 5 % arrive, the Swedes join the Latvians instead. Faiths work the same way. People on the move When people move, they carry their language into the new province's mix. That covers settlers, refugees, the homeless, soldiers coming home and event migrations. - Settlers can carry the court language into any of your own provinces with free tiles, not only colonies. Castilian settlers can go to Toledo. - Refugees count in the mix once they have stayed 2 years, like Andalusi refugees in Fez. - Homeless people drifting next door bring their language, like Galicians into Leon. - Soldiers coming home rejoin their home language. Language policy Each country has one realm-wide Language policy : Let be, Teach or Impose. Teach is the default, and you can override it for any single province. For example, France can keep Teach but set Bayonne to Let be, so drift toward French there is halved. - Let be halves drift toward the court. - Teach keeps drift at its base and makes schools teaching in the court language cost 10 % more upkeep. - Impose doubles drift. It gives the grievance Banned language in every province where most people speak a foreign language, and in provinces where most speak a related language once nationalism there is 0.3 or more. When you switch to it, lords of the affected languages waver one step, foreign-language lords first. That happens once: keeping Impose costs no more loyalty. Impose needs the Printing invention, unless your country has the chancery tradition . At the 1378 start that is Ming, Goryeo, Castile and the Ottomans, who can Impose from the start. Your form of government doesn't matter: a confederation can Impose and an absolute monarchy can Let be. Worked example. Castile has the chancery tradition. Granada is mostly Andalusi Arabic (foreign) and Barcelona mostly Catalan (related) with nationalism 0.1. When Castile sets Impose, Granada gets Banned language and Barcelona does not, and the Andalusi lord Zegri wavers a step, just this once. If nationalism in Barcelona later reaches 0.3, Barcelona gets Banned language too. Banned language ends in a province when the policy there becomes Let be or Teach, when an Own language charter is granted, or when the majority comes to speak the court language. The Own-language charter and other levers The Own language charter means the local language is used in courts and schools. Where it stands: - Foreign rule and Banned language end in that province. - Officials there must be of the local language. - Drift toward the court language stops (Basque people in Bayonne stay Basque). The ruler can grant it, or the province's lords, its towns or a homeland rising can demand it. Revoking it gives Broken charter , as for any charter. Two other levers help. A lord of the local language holding a homeland province ends Foreign rule there, because his language is the people's. And when the ruler marries into a local house, that house's lords count as the same language for loyalty. Officials and lords Officials have a language too: the language of the province where they were hired (an official hired in Breton Rennes is Breton), or of the school they graduated from. You can hire officials of any language in your realm. Official serving among Years to full effect Same language 5 Related 7 Foreign 10 His own language 5 An official of the local language in a foreign-language province keeps Banned language away there, even under Impose; Foreign rule stays. A Breton official in Rennes spares it the Banned language . A province's language doesn't change how many officials and lords your government can support. A foreign-language province costs you only through the longer time your officials need there. Lords: a same-language lord (or a lord of a house your ruler married into) has "shares your language" among his reasons to grow loyal, a foreign-language lord starts one step lower, and a related-language lord has neither. Order and war - A homeland rising draws 8 % of everyone of that language. While nationalism in the homeland is under 0.5 it demands self-rule; at 0.5 or more it demands a new country. - Defenders of the homeland language, rebels included, get +10 % in rough ground: locals know the land. - A garrison captain of another language than his ruler can be bribed. A Breton captain serving a French king can be bribed; an Occitan one can't until nationalism rises. - The war aim Free a people opens on a foreign homeland, or on a related homeland once nationalism there is 0.3 or more. Rennes (Breton, foreign) is open at nationalism 0; Toulouse (Occitan, related) opens only at 0.3. - From the age of revolutions, the war aim Gather our kin (a diplomacy war aim) is offered on a province whose majority is your court language but held by another country, and taking it gives no Foreign rule . In 1820, Piedmont with the court language Italian can take Italian Venetia from Austria this way. In 1700 the war aim isn't offered yet. - From the age of revolutions, the National levy : same-language provinces with nationalism 0.5 or more refill recruits 25 % faster, and foreign-language provinces 25 % slower. Trade, research and diplomacy - Where a trading people is at least 2 % of a province with a market, trade value there rises 10 % and you may have one extra trader from that language. If they are persecuted or expelled, the bonus ends and they go as refugees to a neighbour, who gains it. - A neighbour of the same family counts double toward the 60 % research cap for inventions known by neighbours and trade partners. - Foreign scholars settle first in realms of their own family. - Rulers of the same family start one step warmer, and of the same court language two. After nationalism, a country holding many people of your court language is a natural rival. Languages through history Spread. When an event spreads a family into some provinces, the leading language of that family rises there, or a language set per region in config. If Valencia has Catalan 60 % and Castilian 10 % and an event spreads the latin family there, Catalan rises. The Oromo migrations spread the cushitic family into the Ethiopian highlands, so Oromo rises in each province there. Every 5 years the game runs three checks of its own. The court goes native. If your court language has been under 20 % of your people for 50 years and one other language is over half, the event The court goes native is raised. For example, Qing with the Manchu court and a Han majority. You choose: - Take their language : the majority language becomes the court language, lords of the old language waver a step, and the old language's people become related or foreign (Manchu people become foreign to Qing). - Keep ours : nothing changes and the check runs again in 25 years (raised in 1700, it comes back in 1725). France, with French at 72 % of its people, never sees it. New languages abroad. When settlers of one language have been the majority for 100 years in a map region on another continent than their court, their language there splits into a new creole language, which counts as related to the old court and gets no Foreign rule at once. Settlers on the court's own continent, or for fewer than 100 years, keep their language. Settlers Region Court New language Castilian Mesoamerica Castile Criollo Portuguese Brazil Portugal Brazilian English North America England Anglo-American Dutch Southern Africa Holland Afrikaans Nationalism. Culture reads each province's nationalism support from the event tree and never sets it. - At 0.3 or more, related languages there count as foreign: Foreign rule in their homeland, all drift there × 0.25, and Free a people opens. With Piedmont's Tuscan court, Neapolitans in Naples at 0.3 become foreign. - At 0.5 or more, homeland risings demand a new country, and a released country takes the catalogue record for that people. If none fits, a new country is made, named after the language, with that language at court and the same form of government as the country it broke from. A winning Breton rising in Rennes releases a country with the catalogue's Breton record. Merging languages. A nation-building event can merge named languages into their national language. A nation state, meaning a country whose court language is a national language such as Italian or German, that has kept Impose for 50 years merges the regional languages that belong to its national language, without an event. Italy with an Italian court merges Tuscan and Lombard after 50 years; after 45 it hasn't yet, and Savoy with its French court never does. For event writers. Culture provides the event effects tongue spread , set court tongue , merge tongues and move people (people of the language leave as refugees and settle elsewhere), and the triggers court tongue , tongue share , kin of , cousin of and stranger to . The computer players AI countries pick their Language policy by personality, using the same rules as you: Personality Language policy Levers Hegemon seeker, expansionist Teach, then Impose once they have printing Settlers into conquered border provinces; Gather our kin after 1789 Isolationist, mercantile Let be Own language charters; welcome trading peoples Opportunist Teach Free a people against neighbours with foreign homelands in revolt Zealot Teach Expel trading peoples of another faith When it happens Culture doesn't run monthly. Drift runs once a year in every province after births and deaths. The three history checks run every 5 years. Language % and the Peoples screen are worked out when you open them. Policy changes, charters and event effects happen at once. What you see - Province card, Language line : up to three languages with shares, each with a coloured dot (green same language, yellow related, red foreign, grey trading people), for example "Language French 94 % · Flemish 6 %". Tap it to see this year's drift, which way it pulls and why. - Country card, Language line : your Language %. Tap it to open the Peoples screen. - The Peoples screen : one row per language in your realm, largest first, with its people, relation, provinces, and notes such as homeland, grievances, lords, charter and drift. The Language policy selector sits on top. A big realm (the Ottomans hold 40 languages in 9 families) groups the rows by family, folded shut. Tap a row to light its provinces on the map; long-press to see its lords, its officials and any rising. For France the screen reads: Language People Relation Where Notes French 6.9 m same language 38 prov Occitan 1.6 m related 9 prov homeland, 2 grievances, drifting to French Breton 0.5 m foreign 3 prov homeland, Foreign rule, 1 lord Flemish 0.4 m foreign 4 prov homeland, Foreign rule Basque 0.1 m foreign 1 prov homeland, Own-language charter Jewish 0.02 m trading 6 towns +10 % trade in Paris, Lyon - The Language map mode : provinces coloured by family at far zoom and by language at regional zoom, with a toggle to same language, related and foreign colours for your realm. Homelands of peoples without a country are outlined. In the game now Every province starts with up to three languages from its realm's start record: the court language, the realm's main peoples, and and, in some areas, a local language set by the area rather than the realm. The language most people speak at the start is the province's homeland. - Province card, Language line : the three languages with their dots. Tap it to open this year's drift: the language it drifts toward, why (yours where you have held it 20 years and govern it through an official or lord, else the local majority) and each group's rate with its reasons. Tap again to close it. - Your realm card, Peoples tab (next to Government): the court language, Language % (the same language plus half of the related ones), one fold per family with a row per language (share, people, relation, provinces, where it is the majority, aggrieved provinces) and the Language policy buttons: Let be, Teach (the default at the start) and Impose. Impose needs Printing or a chancery tradition; until then its button is greyed out and says so. The General tab's Language line opens the tab. - Grievances : Foreign rule where most people speak a language foreign to the court in their own homeland, on land taken after the start (land you held at the start never has it, or 394 provinces in 13 realms would start aggrieved in 1444); Banned language where you Impose and most people speak a foreign language. - The Languages map mode : each province coloured by the family of the language most speak, with a key of the largest families. - Drift runs each New Year, so a share moves by a fraction of a point a year: a generation, not a season. There is no list of accepted cultures: who counts as yours comes from same language, related and foreign. Not in yet: per-province homelands, officials' and lords' own languages, schools and town classes speeding drift, people fleeing, charters, and the computer players changing their policy. How it connects - Provinces: stores the language mix, homeland, years held, officials, the Own language charter and the grievances; moves settlers, refugees and soldiers. - Your-Realm: Language % on the country card, lords' loyalty steps, and dynasty changes. - Government: no form limits your Language policy, and a province's language doesn't weigh on the caps; a released country keeps the form of the country it left. - Religion: the same shapes (mix, buildings, charter) and the persecution or expulsion of trading peoples. - Buildings: schools carry a teaching language; Teach raises their upkeep 10 %. - Research: printing for Impose, four inventions speeding drift, family neighbours and scholars. - Historical-Events: families, spread, nationalism support, the new effects and triggers, migrations. - Rebellions: homeland risings and demands for Own language charters. - Warfare: garrison bribes and locals know the land. - Diplomacy: family warmth, natural rivals, marriages, and the war aims Free a people and Gather our kin . - Recruiting: the National levy refill. - Trade: trading peoples' trade value and extra trader. - Subjects: a subject of your court language folds in faster; a foreign-language subject's independence war draws its people. - National-Strengths: language-based strengths such as the chancery tradition. - Revolutions: creole languages and nationalism as signs; regimes set the court language. - Naval: seafaring languages drift slowly on the coast; sailors keep their language. - Music-and-Sound: the music palette follows the court language's family. - Map and Map Modes: the Language map mode, dots and outlines. - The 1378 Start: court languages and each province's starting languages. - Time-and-Turns: the yearly drift slot and the 5-yearly checks. Design-Principles: These are the rules every feature of Pocket Hegemony is designed by. They come from Leroy's direction for the game (decision X-19 in domain/DECISIONS.md ) and from the screen rules already in the specs. Every new or changed feature is checked against them before it is built. Start from how the player uses it Most of the game is played in the screens and cards over the map, not on the map itself. So every feature starts with three questions: where does the player find it, what do they tap, and what do they see back? If the answer is awkward, too many taps, a hidden button, a result that is hard to read, the design changes before any code is written. Group related things together Each subject has one home: one card, one tab or one screen. The country card, for example, has General, Diplomacy, Trade and Army tabs, so war and peace sit with the rest of diplomacy instead of next to the realm's taxes. A feature never spreads its buttons over several unrelated panels. Give the important things an overview Anything the player has to keep track of gets one place that shows its state at a glance and leads to the detail. The Army list shows every commander and their army, a province's Garrison tab shows its troops without a commander, and Needs attention lists every warning and everything waiting for an answer. A new important feature either adds itself to such an overview or gets its own. Check it on a phone Every feature is checked on a phone held sideways as well as on a desktop window: - It fits both the Wide and the Tall layout and stays clear of notches and the home indicator. - Every tap target is at least 44 × 44 points, with 8 points between neighbours. - Nothing needs hover: what hover shows with a mouse, a long press shows on touch. - The map stays visible where it can, with cards as side panels or bottom sheets rather than full screens. Rules that already hold - The map is home: everything opens over it and closes back onto it, and one Back always goes one step back (Screens and navigation). - Settings never change results: they change how the game looks and sounds, never what happens (Settings). - The screen says what is wrong, never what to do: warnings inform, they don't play for you.
Diplomacy: Diplomacy is how countries deal with each other short of fighting, and how they get into and out of wars. You send envoys (your own officials) to other courts, and every request is answered by a plain list of reasons with numbers that the other side adds up: over zero is yes. There is no preview and no hidden score; the answer arrives a month after it is given, with every reason spelled out, so you can see why and try again differently. How it works How two countries stand Two countries stand toward each other in one of nine relation types : Alliance, Friendly, Neutral, Rival, Hostile, At War, Subject, Overlord and Truce. Overlord is never stored; it is read from the other end of a Subject record. Each pair has three independent slots : - Hierarchy : Subject (and so Overlord). - State : at most one of At War, Truce or Alliance per pair. - Stance : one of Friendly, Neutral, Rival or Hostile for each direction, so A can be Friendly toward B while B is Rival toward A. When no stance is stored, the implied stance applies: Hostile at war, Friendly when allied, otherwise Neutral. A missing pair just means nothing is recorded; it is never read as a historical claim of neutrality, and no alliance, subject or rivalry is guessed from friendliness, influence or neighbourhood. A country has at most one direct overlord; chains of subjects are allowed, cycles are not. Every Rival names a contested object (a throne, province, trade city, route, sphere or office). Type Effects Ends by Alliance +50 line; an ally can't be attacked until the alliance is broken breaking, declaring war, making a subject, a country destroyed; never expires Friendly +30 line insult, rivalry, war, decay after 240 months unrefreshed Neutral none any stance change Rival −30 line; AI war target; wars against it please your lords dropping it, the object resolved; lasts at least 120 months Hostile −75 line; blocks alliances; border-raid events (0.02 a month) improving relations, decay to Rival after 120 months At War −100 line; trade between the pair stops peace Subject owned by Subjects independence won, release, annexation Truce −10 line; no war until it expires expiry, breaking it, an alliance, making a subject Some combinations can't exist together: for example an Alliance can't sit with a Neutral, Hostile, At War, Subject or Truce, and At War can't sit with Friendly, Neutral, Alliance, Subject or Truce. A few are allowed only with a note (allies who compete over a contested object, a disloyal subject, a subject competing with its overlord). When effects happen together the order is At War, Truce, Subject, Alliance, Hostile, Rival, Friendly, Neutral, and a newer relation made in play wins over an older one unless the action's own conditions block it. Relations made in play are marked gameplay and never written back into the start data. Diplomatic facts (royal marriage, dynastic claim, territorial claim, trade agreement, secondary tribute, shared ruler, membership, religious authority, and the new protection pledge) only feed reasons; they never create or block a relation. The relation actions move a pair between types: - Declare war needs no Alliance and no Truce with the target, and you can't declare on your own overlord (a subject uses an independence war) or on your own subject (an overlord annexes or releases). It ends Friendly and Neutral stances, creates At War, and sets Hostile where no stance was stored. - Independence war ends the Subject relation, makes both Hostile, and restores the subject if the overlord wins. - Make peace ends the war, makes implied Hostile stances real, and creates a Truce (or a Subject when that is a term). White peace creates a Truce and turns Hostile into Rival, the contested object still open. - Extend truce needs both sides; break truce ends it and makes both Hostile; at expiry a truce ends silently, leaving any stance. - Form alliance needs no Hostile stance either way, no war and no subject tie, and ends any Truce or Neutral. Break alliance ends it with a penalty. - Make subject ends any Alliance, Truce, war and Neutral; release subject makes both Friendly. - Set rival needs a contested object; insult makes the stance Hostile; improve relations moves one step from Hostile to Rival to Neutral to Friendly. - A war between other countries never rewrites a subject relation. A destroyed country loses all its relations. The start dataset holds 503 relations and 128 facts (reference date 20 September 1378), with each Catholic realm's obedience to the Pope in Rome or the Pope in Avignon, and is checked before play. Wars already under way include England against France, Venice against Genoa and its allies, Mamai's Horde against Moscow, Lithuania against the Teutonic and Livonian Orders, Champa against Dai Viet and Ming against the Northern Yuan. The 1444 checkpoint keeps its own 280 relations and 19 facts. Envoys Every envoy is an official sent abroad, and the province he ran is run as if it had no official until he comes back. Countries without officials (chiefdoms, stateless societies) send a lord or elder instead, and a lord away over 12 months loses a step of loyalty. Envoy seats Start 1 Realm of more than 10 provinces +1 (lost at 10 or fewer; residents beyond your seats are then recalled, newest first, while missions finish) G5 Royal chancery +1 (never lost) G8 Resident ambassadors +1 (never lost) A national strength may add 1 Seats are a hard limit on envoys abroad. An envoy's official type helps with what it suits: Official type Better at Bonus Judge peace offers, demands, sworn peace +10 Customs officer trade pacts, passage +10 Chaplain marriages with a ruler of the same faith; anything asked of a same-faith country +10 Steward, Tax collector gifts and loans the gift counts 25 % more Marshal, Warden, Muster master alliances and calls to arms +10 Schoolmaster marriages; courting a foreign lord +10 Master of works nothing extra 0 An envoy with 10 years served adds +5 more, and one resident at a court for 5 years adds +5 to anything asked of it. The road. Envoys travel the army route graph at 2 days per crossing unit (three times march pace), using naval sea times for sea legs. Arrival, one month at court and return are worked out once when sent. A land route through a country at war with you, or one that denied you passage, goes by sea or not at all. Once both countries know T14 telegraphy, a mission is decided the turn it is sent without the envoy leaving home (the answer still comes a month later); marriages and residents still travel. Missions and residents. An envoy carries exactly one task: a mission (one action to one court, decided on arrival, then home) or a residence . With G8 an envoy can stay resident at one court until recalled. A resident adds the tie Resident envoy +5 each season up to +30 (fading over 5 years after he leaves), shows you that country's soldiers, its treasury to the nearest 100 gold and its lords' loyalty, carries any mission there with no travel, and warns you a month ahead when that country is about to declare war on you or your allies. A courtesy visit goes, stays a month, comes back, and leaves the tie Courtesy visit +15 fading over 5 years. Envoys held or lost. If host and sender go to war, the envoy is held until the peace returns him. A demand refused by a Hostile country holds the envoy 1 time in 10, which gives you the war aim Punish . A resident flees home if the country falls to rebels. If the official dies of old age on the road, the seat frees and the mission fails. The envoy carrying a peace is never held. The ledger and standing For each country you have dealt with, your realm keeps a ledger of named ties and wrongs, each with a weight and a fade time or condition. Its total is your standing on a scale of −200 to +200, the same number the event tree calls opinion . The stance or state counts as one line (Alliance +50, Friendly +30, Neutral 0, Rival −30, Hostile −75, At War −100, Truce −10). A ledger holds at most 12 entries; beyond that the smallest merge into "Old matters". A fading entry shrinks in equal yearly steps to zero. Two world-wide counts from Your-Realm also act as reasons. Each Oath broken in the last 30 years is −10 in every count that relies on your word (alliances, pacts, sworn peace, pledges, marriages). Lands taken in the last 20 years drives leagues and is a reason in your neighbours' alliance counts. The reasons count Every yes or no is decided the same way: the asked country lists its reasons, each with a number, and answers yes only when the total is over zero. There is no prediction before asking, and the answer arrives as a letter a month after it is given, yes or no with the full reasons list. Beforehand you can judge only from what you can see: the ledger, the stance, and the other side's soldiers (exact with a resident, otherwise an estimate). Every count holds: - the action's negative base , which says how big the ask is; - standing ÷ 4; - −10 per Oath broken if the action relies on your word; - the envoy's type and years-served reason; - the asked country's personality (−30 to +30 by action); - its ruler's traits (Pious +10 to anything asked by the same faith, Warlike −10 to sworn peace, Greedy +10 to anything with a gift); - a national strength where it says so. Strength is soldiers under arms, with allies who would come counted at half. An ask that binds them to you (alliance, pledge, protection) adds You are stronger than us +10 per full multiple up to +40, or We are stronger than you −10 per full multiple up to −40. A demand adds We cannot beat you +15 per full multiple beyond 1 up to +60, and We have strong friends minus half of that when their allies would defend them. A country already at war adds −30 to any new commitment unless it is against the same enemy. Other common reasons: Too far to matter −15 with no shared border and no shared neighbour, and Very far −15 more when an envoy needs over 60 days; We share an enemy +25 when both are at war with the same country; You threaten our frontier −5 for each province in your Lands taken that borders them; We already have allies −10 for each of their alliances beyond two. Each action adds at most two reasons of its own. Hungary asks Venice, 11 November 1444 (on the 1444 checkpoint world). Hungary and Venice are both at war with the Ottomans; Venice is allied with Florence, a hegemon seeker with high negotiation. Venice's standing toward Hungary is +10 (Same faith). Venice with half its allies has between 1 and 2 times Hungary's soldiers. Hungary's envoy is a Judge with 7 years served. Reason Number Base (alliance) −40 Standing ÷ 4 +2 We share an enemy (Ottomans) +25 We are stronger than you −10 We already have allies 0 Hegemon seeker: alliance with a stronger 0 Negotiation high +10 Total −13: no Hungary then sends Venice a gift of 100 gold, raising standing to +30, and sends a Marshal instead. The total becomes +2, the answer is yes, and Hungary and Venice are allied.
