Revolutions: Revolutions are the great upheavals that change how a country plays: the Dutch Revolt, the Glorious Revolution, the French Revolution, the Meiji Restoration and 32 more. You see one coming on a card that lists its warning signs and how to ease them, you choose how your ruler answers when it breaks out, and the outcome leaves behind a regime: a package of new rules, new buttons and actions you can no longer take. How it works A revolution is not a separate event system. It is an ordinary historical event with one extra block that holds its requirements, signs, sparks, stances and regimes. The fighting itself, when there is any, is a tagged rising handled by Rebellions. Requirements, signs and sparks - Requirements are hard conditions: who, when, and what kind of state. The French Revolution requires a monarchy. Requirements are never shown as signs. If they do not hold, you never see the card, so you are never shown a revolution that cannot happen to you. Venice, a merchant republic, never sees the French Revolution card even with debt above 2,000 gold. - Signs are visible conditions, each with a label and an ease hint. A revolution needs a number of them lit to break out ( need ) and turns its card amber at a lower number ( warn at ). The French Revolution breaks out at 4 of 6 signs and warns at 3. - Sparks multiply the monthly chance once the revolution is ready. For France these are a volcanic winter (×2) and a revolution abroad that won (×1.5). Every revolution also gets the spark "Foreign gold backs the movement" (×2) while a rival is funding it. Signs read numbers you already read elsewhere: grievances in provinces, class shares, your lords' loyalty and land, debt, stability, faith and ideology shares, and lost wars. Four conditions were added for this: Condition What it measures Example grievance The share of a country's (or area's or region's) provinces that have a given grievance France has 10 provinces; 2 are hungry, so "hungry at least 0.2" is true, 1 would not be class share The share of a country's people in one class (farmers, herders, woodsmen, miners, seafolk, craftsmen, market folk, clergy, clerks, scholars, homeless) 12 % of Russians are craftsmen, so "craftsmen at least 0.1" is true lords Land share held by lords rather than officials, the number of lords Wavering or worse, Disloyal or worse, or the count France with 10 provinces, 4 held by lords: land share 0.4 war lost Whether a country made peace on the losing side (gave land, paid, or was made a subject) within a number of years Russia lost and gave land 1 year ago: true within 3 years; 5 years ago: false The game compiles each revolution's trigger as "all requirements, plus at least need of the signs", and adds one selection modifier per spark, so the card and the trigger always agree. A revolution keeps the availability window of the event it extends and never happens outside its era or period window: with every sign lit in 1890, the French Revolution (available 1750 to 1880) still cannot break out. The armistices of 1918 keep their existing trigger instead of a sign checklist. Stages Each revolution moves through stages for each country. Stage What it means Quiet Requirements unmet, or no sign lit Brewing Requirements met, fewer than need signs lit Ready The trigger is true. The event rolls each month by its mean wait times its sparks. The card is red: "may break out any month" Outbreak The event fires with its text and stance options Struggle The option's effects apply. For Fight, a tagged rising appears on the map with its camps Settlement A banner says who won, and the won or crushed effects apply Aftermath The regime applies; waves, émigrés and reactions abroad follow A revolution never fires in the same month its last needed sign lights. It rolls through the normal selection from the next month on, so you always get at least a month with a red card to act. If you ease a sign so that fewer than need are lit, the roll stops: opening the castle stores in France so that "Bread is short in a fifth of the realm" goes dark drops it back to Brewing. Stances Every revolution event offers two to four options, each tagged with a stance. Stance What happens Lead The regime applies at once with no rising. The lords and clergy the regime hurts may rise as the old order camp. Bend A milder regime or a set of reforms applies and some signs end. If enough stay lit, the revolution comes back. Fight A rising tagged with the revolution is raised. If it wins, the option's "rising won" effects apply; if it is crushed, its "rising crushed" effects apply. A crushed rising leaves Bloodshed grievances and the signs stay lit, so it comes back unless you ease them. Path The event's chooser picks a path, and its regimes apply to the countries the option names. A regime on an option can be delayed by a number of years. Each family gives the options their labels; the liberal and national family uses "Proclaim the new order", "Grant a constitution" and "Restore order". Before the French Revolution breaks out you can open "What happens if it breaks out": "Proclaim the new order" leads to the revolutionary republic, "Grant a constitution" to crown and assembly plus emancipation, and "Restore order" to a rising that ends in the revolutionary republic if it wins or in reaction if it is crushed. Camps When a Fight stance raises a rising, the family's camps decide who joins each side, replacing the rebellions join table for that rising only. The revolution camp draws from classes by a monthly join share, plus the lords and the army desertion its family names. In the old order camp, loyal lords send retinues to the ruler and clergy calm their provinces. While the revolution camp holds a province's castle, that province counts as risen. Strength, marching, sieges and melting away follow Rebellions unchanged. Revolution camp join shares per class, per month: Family Who joins Faith homeless 0.30, farmers 0.10, clergy 0.30, craftsmen 0.08, market folk 0.08, only of the movement's faith Estates and towns homeless 0.20, market folk 0.15, craftsmen 0.12, clerks 0.10, scholars 0.05, farmers 0.03 Liberal and national homeless 0.30, scholars 0.25, clerks 0.15, craftsmen 0.12, market folk 0.10, farmers 0.04 (0.10 if hungry) Freedom homeless 0.30, farmers 0.30, craftsmen 0.10, market folk 0.10 Peasant and agrarian homeless 0.30, farmers 0.15, herders 0.10, woodsmen 0.08, miners 0.08, craftsmen 0.04 From above none (old order: clergy 0.10, farmers 0.02) Homeland homeless 0.20, herders 0.10, woodsmen 0.08, farmers 0.06, only of the region's culture War and want homeless 0.30, craftsmen 0.20, seafolk 0.10, miners 0.15, farmers 0.08, scholars 0.10, clerks 0.05 Restorations none (the returning pretender's backers) Each family also has its own lords and army rules. In the faith family, lords of the movement's faith who are Wavering or worse join, and soldiers of that faith desert at 5 % a month. In war and want, soldiers mutiny at 10 % a month while war weariness is above 14. Stopped, not solved A revolution stopped by Bend, by a crushed rising, or by a Path that applies no regime is re-armed. Its card stays up marked "Stopped, not solved". For a grace period of 3 years it cannot break out. After that, whenever need signs are lit again it can break out through the normal selection with its sparks. If the lit signs fall below need , it is disarmed; there is no fixed cooldown to wait out. When it returns it is the same event with the same stances, so a ruler who bent once may fight or lead the second time. A revolution that applied a regime (that won) never re-arms. A re-arming revolution may fire again even if its event is otherwise one-time. Regimes A regime is the package of rules an outcome leaves behind: form of rule, ruler, lords, church, faith, language, levy, land, towns, trade, research, decrees, locks, grievances ended and added, flags, reactions abroad, risks and a one-line "loop" that sums up how it plays. - Form. The regime sets the form of rule from the Government forms. keep leaves the form as it is; old form restores the form held before the last revolutionary regime, which the game remembers. A revolution can grant a form before its era. Crown and assembly gives a constitutional monarchy, or a diet monarchy if the country lacks G14 Written constitution. - Numbers come from the form. A regime never sets its own caps on officials or lords. - One at a time. A country holds one regime, plus add-on regimes that stack on top (emancipation). - Ruler. Kept; deposed (the ruler and heirs go abroad as pretenders); replaced (the rising's leader rules); or elected. - Locks. An action the regime takes away shows greyed out with "Locked by the revolution". The lockable actions are grant fief, sell title, seize land, call the lords, hire companies, crushing taxes, revoke charter, massacre and persecute. - Grievances. A regime ends some grievances and adds others. A revolutionary republic ends Harsh lord and Wrong faith and adds Broken charter . - Flags. revolutionary regime , emigre court and reaction regime are set by regimes; the first is cleared when another regime replaces it. - Reaction. While a country holds the reaction regime, the revolution needs one sign fewer for 20 years. Funding a revolution abroad You can secretly fund a revolution in another country when its card there is at least Brewing; you only see that card where you have a diplomat. While you fund it: - you pay gold every month, 1 % of the target's yearly income; - the target gets the "Foreign gold backs the movement" spark (×2), and if it becomes a rising, its camp's join shares are multiplied by 1.5; - each month there is a 3 % chance you are caught, plus 1 % while the target is at peace and 1 % more if officials run at least half of its provinces. This is the same Fund rebels action diplomacy offers; there is only one. If you are caught, the funding ends, the target gets the opinion reason "Funded a revolution against us" and a reason to fight you, and the card names you. If a funded revolution wins, the new regime starts at +25 opinion of you, unless it is hostile to your form of rule. Its country is bound through the event's role selector, so another country that fits can get the card instead. If its signs never light within its window, it never fires: history is not forced. Ordinary peasant risings, pretender wars and separatist revolts stay in Rebellions, reforms without a struggle are ordinary events, and coups belong to Warfare. What you see - The revolution card on the country screen, about 40 characters wide to fit a phone. For France in 1789 it reads "FRENCH REVOLUTION", brewing, "Breaks out at 4 of 6 signs", with the lit signs first ("Debt above 2,000 gold", "A quarter want a constitution", "The crown is distrusted"), each with how to ease it ("Cut court and army; tax lords"), and the sparks with their multipliers. The bar is neutral, amber at warn at and red at need . - "What happens if it breaks out" opens the stances and the regime each leads to. - Banners. When a revolution breaks out or ends in another country, a one-line banner ("Revolution in France: the Bastille has fallen") appears, but only for neighbours, rivals and Great Powers. Tapping it opens that country's card. - The revolution map mode shades provinces by how many of the revolution's province-level signs they meet and hatches risen provinces in the revolution's colour. - The regime card on the government screen shows the regime's loop line, its decrees as buttons and its locks greyed out. In the game today The 36 historical revolutions read ideologies, legitimacy and ages the game does not track yet, so the first slice gives every realm one revolution of its own, built from the two oldest families. A monarchy with no hunger has an Estates and towns revolution (as the Fronde and the Comuneros); a realm that is hungry, or not a monarchy, has a Peasant and agrarian one (as the Tay Son and Donghak risings). - Signs (3 of 6 to break out, amber at 2): Heavy taxes in a quarter of the realm; Hungry in a fifth; a tenth rioting or plotting; two or more lords Wavering or worse; debt above a year's income; rebels holding your land, or rebels who won against you in the last 5 years. Under the reaction regime one sign fewer is enough, for 20 years. - Breaking out : a red card breaks out on a roll of 1 in 12 a month, 1 in 6 while two or more lords are Disloyal, never in the month it turned red and never within 3 years of the last revolution, Bend or crushed rising. - Where you see it : the Stability plaque in the top bar carries a mark while a revolution brews (amber) or may break out (red); tap it for your Realm book's Overview, where the Revolution block under the four pillars lists the lit signs first, each with a button to the tab that eases it, and folds out what each answer would do. - When it breaks out : a full-screen card asks how you answer, and End turn waits for it. - Estates: Share power makes you a diet monarchy (League of towns, crushing taxes locked); Grant charters fixes the tax at light for 10 years wherever it is heavy, and the revolution is stopped, not solved; Break them raises a town rising in your most restless province. - Agrarian: Divide the land (Land to the villages: no more fiefs granted, every lord loses a loyalty step); Cut taxes and open the granaries (light tax for 10 years where it is heavy, castle granaries opened where people are hungry; stopped, not solved); Crush the bands raises a hunger rising. - The struggle : the rising plays as any other on the map. If it wins, an estates revolution makes you a merchant republic with an elected ruler; an agrarian one puts the rising's leader on your throne, your house goes abroad as pretenders, every lord wavers and tax stays light for 10 years. If it is beaten, starves or is bribed away, the Reaction follows: bloodshed where they rose, and the revolution comes back sooner. If you grant or talk out its demand, it is stopped, not solved. - Rebels who win : an ordinary rising that wins against you lights the rebels sign, and if your card is then red, or the rebels took your capital's castle, the revolution has won at once. - Government tab : the regime under your form, its loop line and since when, your ruler, the form before the revolution, and its locks greyed out. Locked orders are refused with "locked by the revolution". - Other realms : computer realms go through the same rules and pick Fight, Bend or Lead by weight, Fight more often when their armies outnumber the rising. A neighbour's revolution is a line in your News. How it connects - Historical events: revolutions are events; this adds four conditions, the regime and lock effects, two new effect tiers and four flags (not merged yet). - Rebellions: Fight raises a tagged rising; camps replace the join table; won and crushed hooks. - Government: regimes set forms, in any era, and restore the old form. - Diplomacy: "Different form of rule", the counter-revolution reason, and the funding action. - Subjects: settler colonies going independent through a Disloyal colony. - Culture: nationalism thresholds read by liberal and national signs; regimes can set the court language. - Religion: the faith wave, and church events that follow a revolutionary regime. - National strengths: a won revolution may overcome a weakness or grant a legacy (a hook only). - Warfare: generals growing too big, and a winning general switching the regime. - Provinces: grievances and class shares feed the signs; regimes end and add grievances. - Your realm: lords' loyalty and land, stability and debt; locks on fiefs and titles. - Research: G14 Written constitution decides the crown and assembly form. - Map and Map Modes: the revolution map mode. - Screens and navigation: banner, card and regime card. - Music and sound: the revolution music tag. Each month The game evaluates requirements and signs for every revolution and country and sets stages and card colours; for Ready revolutions the events system rolls the selection; re-arm grace periods tick; funding is charged and the caught chance is rolled; delayed regimes apply; decree limits tick. Numbers Every balance value here is a provisional placeholder. Key Value revolutions.<id .signs.need per revolution (the "breaks out at" column) revolutions.<id .signs.warn at per revolution revolutions.<id .sparks[].mult per revolution Event selection.mean years per event rearm.grace years 3 years families.<id .camps.revolution.joins the join table above families.<id .wave.amount the wave table above counter revolution.years 25 years (proposed) counter revolution.opinion −50 (proposed) generals.too big mult ×2 (proposed) emigre.funding per year not given yet foreign backing.mult 2 foreign backing.joins mult 1.5 foreign backing.cost 1 % of the target's yearly income a month foreign backing.catch chance 3 % a month foreign backing.win opinion +25 reaction.need reduction 1 sign for 20 years Settled details - A revolution's rising starts as a rising, not a great revolt. Its size comes from the event and the province's recruits, split between the camps. - Signs read real numbers: debt in gold, grievance counts, lords' loyalty and school seats. "Integration strain" is the share of your provinces with Foreign rule . - American-style colony revolutions read whether the colony is disloyal to its overlord. - Regimes do not grant or remove national strengths. - Counter-revolution: monarchies' opinion falls by 50 and they hold a reason to fight for 25 years, unless the regime sets its own values. It replaces the usual "different form of rule" penalty instead of adding to it. - Restorations happen only through their own events: the restoration of the old order (1660 to 1815) and the émigré events. - A wave is a one-off change in the realms bordering the revolution's country and in its region. Faith waves use religion's faith wave. - When a revolution sets a regime, the regime decides the form of rule. Crown and assembly keeps its form later on. - The armistices of 1918 are one-time events with no revolution card. - A decree whose cost is part of its effect shows that effect as its cost. - Revolutions "from above" are decisions you are offered; nobody rises. - The catch-chance additions for peace and officials are provisional and may still be tuned. Still open - Seven new historical sources still need to be checked by a person. The offline build validates the layer, merges it into a scratch copy of the event tree, runs the event tree validator, and writes the catalogue, runtime JSON and the event tree patch without ever editing the tree itself. Saving: Saving in Pocket Hegemony is built so that you never lose more than the orders you gave since your last End turn, even if your phone kills the app without warning. Saves work the same on every platform, keep loading after updates, and can follow you between your phone, tablet, Steam Deck and the web through an optional account, or as a file you export yourself. Where you find it Tap the three-line button at the top left of the map (or press Esc ) to open the game menu: Return to the map, Save, Load, Settings and Exit to main menu. - Save shows the new save's name, already filled in with your realm and date, and a Save button. Under it are this campaign's saves; Save over asks "Replace?" right in the row. "Saved." shows over the map when it is done. While the week plays, Save waits until it has played. - Load lists every save on this device, newest first, with its map crop, banner, date and when it was saved. Each campaign's first line is "Where you left off". Tap a line to Load or Delete it; Delete asks first. Going back to an earlier save of the campaign you are playing asks "Leave … unsaved?" when weeks have passed since your last save. - Where you left off is kept after every week and when you leave, so Exit to main menu and Continue on the start screen bring you straight back. - Autosaves are set in Settings → Gameplay. On the web, saves are kept in your browser's storage on this device. How it works The principles - Only at a turn boundary. A save is the world at the start of a turn plus the orders you have queued so far. It is never a point halfway through a turn. - Lose almost nothing. At worst you lose the orders given since your last End turn. - Write once. Every save file is written once and never changed. A new save gets a new file name; replacing means writing the new file first and then removing the old one. - One format everywhere. A save made on any platform opens on any other. - Old saves keep loading. Every released format has a migration to the next and a test save in the repository. - Only game state. Rules, map shapes and art come from the game itself. Settings, purchases and achievement progress live elsewhere. Kinds of save Saves are grouped by campaign : one new game is one campaign, with a random id. Kind When it is written How many are kept In the Load list Resume After every End turn, and on pause, quit, exit to the main menu or suspend (backgrounding writes only the orders journal) 1 per campaign, plus the one before as a backup No; it is what Continue opens Autosave At the start of a turn in which a month on your autosave interval begins Your choice of 1, 3 or 5 per campaign, oldest rotated out Yes, marked "Auto" Manual When you tap Save, with a name Up to 20 per campaign and 100 in total Yes Ironman After every End turn and on every exit (Save and quit, Exit to main menu, closing the app), in an ironman campaign 1 plus a backup Yes, as the campaign itself Exported When you tap Export; the file leaves the game No limit Imported files join the Manual saves Autosave options. The interval can be every month, every 6 months (January and July), every 12 months (each January) or off; the default is every 12 months. An autosave is written at the start of the turn in which that month begins, so even "every month" writes about once every 4 turns. You can keep 1, 3 or 5 autosaves per campaign; the default is 3. Turning autosaves off stops only the rotating autosaves. An ironman campaign writes no rotating autosaves, only its ironman save. If something goes wrong, "Restore the last autosave" on the failure screen opens your Resume save, or your newest autosave if the Resume save is damaged. The Resume save cannot be turned off. Continue opens the newest Resume or Ironman save across all your campaigns, whether it was made on this device or arrived from the cloud. If it came from another device, the button says so: "Continue: Portugal, March 1512 (from Steam Deck)". The Load screen lists campaigns first, each with its nation banner, nation name, in-game date, turn, play time and a small map crop. Opening a campaign lists its saves newest first, each marked autosave or ironman and with the device that made it. The list reads only each file's header, so it fills quickly without unpacking whole saves. Saving by hand Save in the game menu shows the campaign's slots with "New save" at the top and your manual saves below. A new save is named after your nation and date ("Castile, May 1492"); renaming is optional, so you never need a keyboard with a controller. Picking an existing save asks "Replace?". At the slot limit, Save asks which one to replace and never removes one silently. Deleting a save from the Load screen asks for confirmation. The game keeps its messages short and plain: Situation What you see A save is written A small "Saved." toast, no dialog Not enough space "There isn't enough space on this device to save. Free some space, or delete old saves." A save from a newer version "This save is from a newer version of Pocket Hegemony. Update the game to open it." A damaged save "This save is damaged. The previous save from Dec 1511 was opened instead." A locked nation "Portugal is part of the full game. Unlock it to continue this campaign." The Resume save and the orders journal When you end a turn, the engine writes the Resume save for the new turn in the background, and you can give orders while it writes. While you give orders, the game keeps an orders journal : the orders queued since the turn began, in the same form End turn sends them. It is written whenever the app is backgrounded, suspended or closed, and every 30 seconds while orders are changing. When you come back, the game loads the Resume save and puts the journal's orders back in the queue, giving you exactly the state you left. If the journal's turn number or Resume save hash does not match, it is ignored. The journal is never synced. A choice you make at a before-the-battle stop also goes into the journal with its day, so the turn plays out the same way when it is replayed. The journal is written on these platform events: Platform Events iOS pause and appStateChange (inactive) Android pause Desktop window close , before-quit , and suspend (Steam Deck and Steam Machine suspend this way) Web visibilitychange (hidden) and pagehide If a turn is being processed when the app goes to the background, nothing new is saved: the previous Resume save and journal stay, and the turn is processed again on resume. On desktop, quitting waits for the write, up to 2 seconds. Writing safely Every file is written in four steps: serialise and compress in the engine worker; write to a temporary file in the same folder; flush and rename it to its final name (a single transaction in IndexedDB on the web); and only then remove what it replaces. The newest two Resume saves are always kept, so if the newest is damaged the game falls back to the one before. The save file A save is one binary .phsave file: 1. the magic "PHSV" (4 bytes); 2. a container version (uint16); 3. the header length (uint32); 4. the header, as uncompressed JSON; 5. a chunk table: the count, then for each chunk its id, version, offset, length and CRC-32; 6. the chunks, each compressed with deflate. Compression uses a small bundled deflate library rather than the browser's own, so output is identical on every platform, including iOS 15 web views. The header holds the save id, campaign id, kind, name, when it was saved, device, platform, game version, format version, rules hash, map hash, turn, date, player nation, the ironman flag, play time, the campaign options (difficulty, events, end date), the tier (nation, and whether it needs the full game), the world hash and a 96 × 64 thumbnail. Chunks. Each system gets its own chunk with its own version, so a new system adds a chunk without touching the others. Chunk What it holds core Turn, date, random number state, game options, the player's nation ids The province, nation and commander id lists provinces, nations Their changing fields armies Live armies only, with their routes events Events fired, flags set, pending choices and cooldowns history The realm timeline for the ledger and end screens orders Queued orders, only in a Resume save made during a turn later: diplomacy, subjects, religion, culture, government, trade, ai, … One per system Only changing state is saved, never anything from the build (adjacency, terrain, water, rivers, province shapes). Arrays are stored as raw bytes and always indexed through the ids chunk, never by position in the build's data. Keeping saves working across updates - The format version goes up whenever any chunk's layout changes. Loading an older save runs every migration step in order, each a pure function from one version's chunks to the next, then validates the result. - If the rules or the map changed, the game then matches provinces and nations by id, applies the map's rename table (old province id to new ids with shares) for split or merged provinces, applies the nation table to dropped nations, and gives new fields their default. A dropped nation with no entry leaves its provinces unowned and loads with a warning in the log, not an error. - A save from a newer version never opens. - A balance patch applies from the next turn on with the saved random state: it changes outcomes from then on but never corrupts the save. - Each release adds at least two saves (one early game, one late game) to the test saves. Every test run loads every save from every earlier release and plays a turn. A release does not ship if any old save fails, and the changelog says when the format changes. Cloud saves Cloud saves run on Pocket Hegemony's own server, so one optional account carries a campaign across Steam, iPhone, iPad, Android and the web. The game still plays fully offline. - No conflicts by design. Files are named <campaignId /<savedAt -<saveId .phsave , so two devices that played offline simply end up with both sets. The Load screen shows them all, marked with the device that made each, and Continue picks the newest. Two devices continuing the same non-ironman campaign make two lines of play, and that is not an error. - What syncs. All Manual saves, the latest Resume and Ironman save per campaign, and the newest autosave per campaign. Older autosaves, the backup Resume save and the orders journal stay on the device. - Deleting a campaign deletes it from the cloud too. A removed save gets a tombstone so other devices learn of it, and its bytes are purged 30 days later. - Signing in is with email and password. You get a short-lived access token and a long-lived device token, kept in the platform's secure storage (Keychain, Keystore, or Electron's safe storage). Each device appears in your account's device list and can be signed out from any other. Password reset by email and account deletion (which deletes every save) are offered. Sign in with Apple, Google and Steam come later; if Google is offered on iOS, Apple will be too. Sign-in is offered from a Cloud saves row in Settings and a "Sign in to sync" prompt on the Load screen, never as a wall before playing. - When it syncs. On launch and when you return to the app, the game fetches changes since its last position, headers first so the Load screen fills at once. A save's bytes download only when you open it, or in the background for the newest Resume save. Every written save is queued for upload; the queue survives restarts and empties oldest first when online, retrying with back-off. Backgrounding does nothing extra for the cloud, so those few seconds go to the orders journal. "Sync on Wi-Fi only" (off by default) stops syncing on a metered connection. - Server checks. Each upload is checked for size (2 MB cap), magic, CRCs, and that its header matches. Each account has a quota of 300 saves and 200 MB; at the quota the game asks you to delete old saves, and the server never drops one on its own. There is a rate limit per account and per device. Later, the server can load a save with the engine and check its world hash before trusting it, for example for a leaderboard. - Saves, not purchases. A campaign synced from one store opens on another device only if its nation is unlocked there. The server keeps a table of the header fields the Load screen needs and stores the file bytes in object storage, not in the database. Its interface: Request What it does GET /api/saves?since=<cursor Headers and tombstones changed since the cursor, plus the new cursor PUT /api/saves/{saveId} Upload one save; rejected for an existing id unless the bytes match GET /api/saves/{saveId} Download the bytes DELETE /api/saves/{saveId} Tombstone one save DELETE /api/campaigns/{campaignId} Tombstone every save of a campaign POST /api/campaigns/{campaignId}/ironman-head Claim the ironman line Store backups, Export and Import Platform Free backup Steam Steam Auto-Cloud on the save folder, one cloud folder for Windows, macOS and Linux, 500 MB and 2,000 files for the synced set only, Dynamic Cloud Sync on so a suspended Deck uploads Android Auto Backup of the synced set (within its 25 MB limit), excluding the orders journal iOS and iPadOS The device's own iCloud backup includes the save folder Web Saves live in IndexedDB; the game asks for persistent storage. Signing in is the only way to keep web saves beyond the browser Play Games saved games and an iCloud Documents container are not used. Export writes a .phsave file through the share sheet on phones or a save dialog on desktop. Import (file picker, or opening the file from Files, Drive or a download) checks its magic, CRCs and world hash and adds it to your Manual saves, with the same nation-lock check as any save. Free tier and full game On phones the free download and the full game are the same app, so saves carry over with nothing to do; buying the unlock removes the lock. Each header records your nation and whether it needs the full game. Loading a locked nation's save without the full game shows the unlock screen instead of failing, and never deletes the save. If a purchase is refunded or revoked, the saves stay and those nations ask to be unlocked again. With the Steam demo and the full game on the same computer, the full game finds the demo's saves on first launch and copies them into its own folder, and Steam Cloud keeps them from then on. A signed-in demo player's saves sync to the full game on any computer or phone; without an account, Export and Import do the same. Each save records which app wrote it (free, demo or full game) but no list of limits, so the full game simply opens a demo save with no limits. Ironman - Chosen only when a campaign starts, and it cannot be turned off. - No manual Save, no Load of earlier points, no console or debug tools. - Export is allowed as a backup. Importing an ironman save starts it on this device; the copy on the old device is then no longer the newest. Importing an ironman save needs a connection: offline you see "Connect to import an ironman save." - The server accepts an ironman upload only if the save it names as its parent is still the campaign's newest ironman save. Otherwise the second device is told to load the newer game first. - If two devices played the same ironman campaign offline and the line has split, the game asks once: "Keep the game from Steam Deck (June 1530) or from this phone (Feb 1528)?", recommends the one further along, and removes the other line. - If an ironman save is damaged, its backup opens and you are told; you roll back at most one turn. Integrity Every chunk has a CRC, and loading recomputes the world hash, so damaged or edited files are caught. Saves are not encrypted. A save that fails the hash check opens only outside ironman, after a warning, and is marked as modified. The header carries the ironman flag, the modified mark and four flags for Achievements: ironman unbroken, cheat marked (the game has no cheats or console, so this is the modified mark), switched country, and began as the tutorial. Your campaign options (difficulty, events, end date, AI temper, fog of war and the music-era rule) are saved with the campaign; tutorial progress and Needs attention mutes belong to your player profile and sync with it, not with any save. A damaged or cut-short save is rejected cleanly and the previous save is opened or offered. Bug reports and tests Send a report, on the failure screen, attaches the Resume save and the orders journal, and sending is always your choice. Before release the save code must pass: every test save loads, migrates and plays a turn; save, load and save again gives identical chunks and the same world hash; a file cut short at any byte is rejected cleanly with the previous save offered; killing the app during a write leaves the old save intact (desktop and both phone platforms); backgrounding, killing and relaunching on a real iPhone and Android phone resumes with the queued orders; and two devices with cloud on, played offline and reconnected, show both lines of play, with the one prompt for ironman. What you see - Continue on the main menu, with "(from <device )" when the save came from elsewhere. - The Load screen: campaigns first, then their saves, each marked with the device that made it, and a "Sign in to sync" prompt. - Save in the game menu with "New save" and your manual saves; "Replace?" when saving over one. - The "Saved." toast and the plain messages above. - The Cloud saves row and "Sync on Wi-Fi only" in Settings, and the autosave interval and count rows. - The ironman split prompt, asked once. - The unlock screen for a locked nation's save. How it connects - How a turn works: the turn must finish deterministically from the saved random state; turn number, date and orders. - Screens and navigation: Continue, Load, Save, toasts and messages, the app lifecycle, the unlock screen and the split prompt. - Settings: the autosave values, the Cloud saves row, Wi-Fi only and sign-in; personal settings ride the same account. - Achievements: reads the ironman flag and the modified mark, and asks for more flags. - Tutorial and help: tutorial progress and Needs attention mutes live in your player profile, apart from saves. - The 1378 start: campaign options, ironman and the player's nation at a new game. - Map and Map Modes: the map hash, province ids and the rename table. - Historical events: the events chunk. - Every system (Provinces, Your realm, Warfare, Diplomacy …) owns its own chunk with its own version and migrations. Saving never changes the simulation. The computer players' state is saved like anything else. Numbers From save-config.example.yaml . Key Value Status format.extension / format.magic .phsave / PHSV fixed format.thumbnail 96 × 64 fixed kinds.resume.keep 2 (newest plus backup) fixed kinds.autosave.interval months 12 decided default kinds.autosave.interval options 1, 6, 12, off fixed kinds.autosave.keep / keep options 3 / 1, 3, 5 default kinds.manual.max per campaign 20 provisional kinds.manual.max total 100 provisional kinds.ironman.keep 2 fixed orders journal.safety interval seconds 30 provisional budgets.file kb start / file kb late 400 KB / 2048 KB targets budgets.write ms / journal write ms 300 ms / 20 ms targets budgets.header read ms / load ms 5 ms / 1500 ms targets cloud.server.max save mb 2 provisional cloud.server.quota saves / quota mb 300 / 200 provisional, to decide later cloud.server.tombstone purge days 30 provisional cloud.server.wifi only default false fixed cloud.store backups.steam 500 MB, 2,000 files platform ironman.conflict / recommended choice ask once / furthest turn fixed integrity.modified saves allowed outside ironman with a warning fixed desktop quit wait seconds 2 s provisional kinds.autosave.every 6 months January, July provisional The budgets are targets for a low-end Android phone, still to be confirmed by the performance design. Still open - The cloud quota (300 saves, 200 MB per account) is a starting point until real save sizes are measured, and which social sign-ins ship at launch is a store decision. For developers - Spec: domain/saves/spec.md , requirement code SAVE (SAVE-001 to SAVE-104). - Features: domain/saves/features/ (save-kinds-and-continue, saving-by-hand, resume-and-orders-journal, safe-writing, save-file-format, migrations, cloud-sync, backups-export-import, free-tier-saves, ironman, integrity-and-testing). - Code: packages/engine/src/domain/saves/ . The engine core has packages/engine/src/protocol.ts ( newGame with seed and nation only, endTurn with orders) and hashWorld in packages/engine/src/hash.ts ; the save and load requests are still to be added. Test saves go in packages/engine/test/saves/ .
Screens-and-Navigation: This page covers every screen of Pocket Hegemony, from the boot logo to the final result of a campaign, and how you move between them with touch, mouse, keyboard or controller. The idea is simple: in a campaign the map is home, everything else opens over it and closes back onto it, and one Back action always takes you one step back. How it works The principles - The map is home. While a campaign is loaded, every screen is either a card over the map or a full screen that closes back onto the map. The map is never unloaded. - One stack, one Back. All screens live on one stack. The system back gesture, the on-screen Back button, Esc and the controller's B button all pop the top of it. - Never more than three steps from the map. - One tap to play. From a cold start with a campaign in progress you reach your map with one tap on Play. - Ask only when something is lost. First-run questions appear only once. Confirmations appear only where you would lose something (leaving without saving, overwriting a save). - Layout by shape, not by device. Screens follow the shape of the window. - Every input works everywhere. Every screen works with only a controller and with only touch. Nothing exists only as a hover or only as a long press. Starting the game Boot. A cold start shows the pixel logo on parchment with the hourglass turning while the map, sprites and engine load. No studio logos, no video. On iOS and Android the native launch screen shows the same logo. If loading takes under 0.6 seconds the boot screen still stays 0.6 seconds; otherwise it stays only as long as loading takes. If loading fails (a missing file, or the engine worker will not start and the fallback also fails), you get the failure screen. First run. The first time the game runs, it asks its first-run questions before the start screen, each as one card with one choice, and never again. If your device language is one the game has, it is used silently (you can change it in Settings); otherwise a card asks. Where something needs consent (crash reports, and counting how far players get in the tutorial), one consent card asks for both, with both off until you turn them on; where nothing on a store needs consent, it does not appear. There are only these two first-run questions. The game never asks you to sign in before play, and it plays offline. Start screen. The game opens on the start screen with its menu already showing; there is no "Tap to start". Behind it the real map pans slowly at region zoom, close enough to see provinces, towns and castles. With a campaign in progress it pans over your realm in its current borders and season, read from the latest save's summary; otherwise it picks one of a handful of regions of the 1378 world. The map behind takes no input and runs no simulation, and with Battery saver on it keeps moving at the lower frame rate. The title music starts on your first touch, click, key or button. The menu has two groups: Group Entry When it shows Where it goes Column Play (large, wax-red, focused first) Always With a campaign in progress it shows the realm's banner, name and date ("France · May 1503") and loads the newest save; otherwise New campaign Column New campaign While a campaign is in progress New campaign Column Load While any save exists Load Column Tutorial Until the tutorial is finished, then under More The tutorial's chapter list Icon row Settings Always Settings, over the start screen Icon row Achievements Always Achievements Icon row Wiki Always This wiki, in your browser; the game stays where it was Icon row More Always Almanac, Credits, Unlock (Buy the full game in the Steam demo), and Tutorial once finished Icon row Quit Desktop and Steam only; phones have none Closes the game The version number sits small in the lower right corner. Back on the start screen leaves the app on Android and does nothing elsewhere. Exit to main menu in a campaign brings you back here, with the map panning over the realm you just left. On a phone in landscape the logo sits top left, the column and icon row fill the left third on a parchment band, and the map pans across the rest; on a tablet held upright the map fills the top half and the menu sits below it. Play is at least 56 points tall, everything else at least 44, and each icon has its name under it. New to Pocket Hegemony? The very first time you press Play, with no campaign yet, the game asks once: Play the tutorial (focused), Guided campaign, or I know the way. The tutorial starts at its first chapter; Guided campaign opens New campaign with the goals list for your first year switched on; I know the way opens New campaign without it. See Tutorial and help. The free tier. The free mobile download and the Steam demo let you play the Ottomans and France, with nothing else held back. They show a small "Full game" ribbon beside the logo on the start screen that leads to Unlock, never as a pop-up. No version of the game shows ads. The Unlock screen offers one purchase, the full game, which unlocks every realm; it shows the store's price and a Buy button, and on phones also Restore purchases. New campaign One screen in three steps, with a strip at the top ("Realm · Options · Begin"). Back moves one step back, and from step 1 returns to the start screen without asking. The nation select music plays, its lead voice changing with the highlighted realm. 1. Realm. Choose a realm on the map at world zoom, with filters (region, difficulty, free or locked) and a short list of suggested realms. Choosing a region frames it on the map and lists every realm there by name, one row each. Tapping a realm shows its card with its strengths at a glance and one line, Ways to grow (The 1378 start). A locked realm shows a padlock and a button to Unlock; coming back from a purchase returns you to step 1 with that realm still chosen. Quick start skips straight to Begin with the last options used and the realm you last tapped (or the first suggested one). 2. Options. Difficulty, AI aggression, fog, historical or free events, ironman, and the end date, with presets that fill the whole step. The end date is 31 August of any year from 1494 to 1939; 31 August 1939 is the default. 3. Begin. A summary card (banner, ruler, capital, start date, options) and one big Begin button. Load and loading The Load screen lists every save in one list, newest first (not grouped by campaign), each with banner, realm, in-game date, the real date saved and an autosave or ironman mark. Tapping one shows its card with Load and Delete. Loading from the main menu needs no confirmation. Loading from the game menu with unsaved turns first asks "Leave <date unsaved? · Save first · Leave · Cancel". The loading screen shows a tip from the one tips table, picked to fit your realm and date (tips are tagged by era, region and whether they are for new players). Tap, or press left and right, for another. The bar shows the real loading steps ("Reading the save", "Drawing the borders", "Waking the courts"), not a fake timer. While the game works, the rider gallops, the road runs under the hooves, a shine runs along the bar and the dots after the step count up, even while the world is being built, so you can always see it has not frozen. When loading finishes, the game goes straight to the map without asking for a tap, but keeps a tip on screen at least 2 seconds after it appeared. The load-and-resume music plays. The four layers of a campaign Layer Examples How it closes Map Home Back opens the game menu Cards Province, army, commander, country, lord, castle, rebellion, sea zone Back, ✕, tapping empty map, or minimising Full screens Realm book, levy, Food policy, Tax, battle viewer Back or ✕ returns to whatever was below Modals Event, peace offer, confirmation, game menu Only their own buttons; Back means "decide later" where that is allowed A modal accepts no input to the screens below until it is answered or put off. The map - Top bar: realm name and banner (opens the country card), the date, gold with its monthly change, and levies. On a phone it holds at most five plaques; the rest move into the country card. - Tool column on the right edge: map mode, go to capital, your commanders and sound, two buttons wide on a phone held sideways. Achievements and Settings are in the game menu, whose button carries a dot while an achievement waits to be looked at. - End turn (the hourglass, lower right) carries a badge counting the items on the Attention screen. Tapping the badge, or the controller's "next" button, opens the Attention screen. - Auto (just above End turn) lets the weeks play one after another in a single-player campaign; a tap stops it at the end of the current week. See Time and Turns. - Attention bell next to the date lights while the Attention screen holds a warning, and opens it. It is the only place the game warns you; there is no advisor. - Game menu button , a small three-line icon in the upper left next to the banner. - The local zoom's tile-row view is still the map, not a separate screen. Cards A tap on the map only selects, and never moves or zooms the map; the thing's name appears on a tab in the lower left. Army banners take big taps, a tap on a commander in the Army list selects his army, and several armies can be selected at once. Tapping the tab, or tapping the thing again, opens its card. Minimising a card shrinks it back to that tab. When a card opens another card (a province, then its owner's country, then a commander), or you switch tabs, the screen you left goes on a history of up to 20 screens. The arrow at the left of the card's header (beside Minimise and the cross) is Back: it returns to the screen before, on the tab you left it, and shows only while there is somewhere to go back to. Your phone's back gesture does the same. A redraw as the week plays adds nothing, and closing the card, or tapping empty map, clears the history. A line that "opens its gain and lose list" opens it inside the card as a fold-out, not as a new screen. How a card sits depends on the shape: Shape Card Short wide (phone landscape) Full height on the left 45 % of the screen; the map stays live on the right, recentred so the selected thing is not hidden Tall A bottom sheet at 55 % height, dragged up to full height or down to a peek strip Large A side sheet 380 px wide at UI scale 1 A country card has the tabs General, Diplomacy, Trade and Army, and opens on General. A province card has a Garrison tab for the troops there without a commander. The Realm book Your own realm's card is the Realm book. Tap your banner or a plaque in the top bar and it opens beside the map, on the page that holds what you tapped (the gold plaque opens Economy, Treasury). Its pages are grouped into six sections, each answering one question, so you never scan a long row of tabs. A new system adds a page inside a section, never a seventh section. Section Pages The question it answers Realm Overview, Government, Heritage, Score How is my realm doing? Economy Treasury, Trade, Food Where do my money and food come from? Lands Provinces, Officials, Lords, Colonies, Hunting grounds (tribal realms) Who runs which land? Military Army, Navy What can fight? Diplomacy Diplomacy Who are my friends and foes? Research Research, Peoples What do we study and believe? The Overview (Realm's first page) is the whole realm on one screen: your capital, then one tile for each other section with its key line (gold and gold a month, provinces and people, armies and men, war or peace, what you study), then your ruler and heir, the score and Stability's four pillars. A tile with a red edge says what waits on you ("2 provinces hungry", "1 new land to fill", "An answer waits", "Choose what to study"), and tapping it opens the page that holds it. What the old General tab repeated from other pages (government form, faiths and languages, lands by ground, heritage, the fallen, neighbours) now lives only on its own page. The six sections are one row of icons with their names under the card's title, in every shape; a section with several pages shows them in a second, lower row. Tapping a section opens the page you last looked at there. A red seal on Diplomacy means an offer or an envoy waits for your answer. Turn reports and battle replays live in the News (the scroll button in the top bar), which took the place of the old Chronicle. Another realm's card keeps its own tabs: General, Diplomacy, Trade, Army and Heritage. Show on map (on a screen that points at an army or province) closes the book, moves the camera and opens that card; Back returns to the book on the same tab and scroll position. A book screen opened from a card (Levy from a province card) stacks on the card, and Back returns to the card. The game menu The game menu opens from its button, from Back on an empty map, from Esc, or from the controller's Menu button. It is a modal over the dimmed map: a menu, not a pause screen, because the game is turn-based. In order: Return to the map (focused first), Save, Load, Settings, Almanac, Achievements, Exit to main menu, and Quit (desktop and Steam only). In ironman, Save reads "Save and quit" and there is no Load. During the tutorial, Skip this chapter, Chapter list and Leave the tutorial come right after Return to the map. Once a campaign can no longer earn achievements, the entry reads "Achievements (off for this campaign)". Campaign rules are shown, read only, inside Settings. Settings opens as an overlay and returns to the game menu. Exit and Quit ask only if there are unsaved turns; in ironman they save and exit without asking. The turn 1. Orders. The map is live. End turn ends the turn with one tap, with a confirmation only if Settings turns it on. While any event is unanswered, End turn shows the event's scroll icon with the count instead of the hourglass, and tapping it opens the first unanswered event instead of ending the turn. 2. Turn in progress. Your orders for the turn are written down before it runs, so together with the last save the world before the turn is kept and killing the app mid-turn loses nothing. The map stays visible and can be panned and zoomed, orders are frozen, the hourglass turns, armies march along their routes and borders change as results arrive. If a turn takes longer than 1.5 seconds, a small parchment strip says what is being worked out ("The courts of Europe deliberate…"). 3. Battles. Each turn is one week: End turn plays 7 days, and the top bar shows the date with its day, such as "27 September 1378". The week plays out day by day. When one of your armies or fleets meets an enemy, the map flies there and the battle view opens: both sides, their commanders, the ground, how far the battle has got, and its standing orders. While any of your battles runs, time slows to steps of 4 hours, six a day, and you watch it round by round. At any step you can change the standing orders for that battle or press Retreat. You cannot skip to the result. If several of your battles run at once, a battle switcher lists them with each one's progress, and you can jump between them. When all of them have ended, a result card (who won, men lost, the one-line reason) with Carry on sends time back to whole days until your next battle or the end of the week. Battles between other realms never slow the game; they appear on the map and, if they matter to you, in the turn report. Every battle can be watched again from the turn report and the Chronicle. 4. Events open one at a time as modal cards (picture, text, two or three options, each showing its effects on tap or focus), in date order. Look at the map shrinks the event into the badge on End turn so you can check something first. Nothing ever answers an event for you. See Historical events. 5. News. What happened goes in the News log, which never opens by itself. Tap the scroll button in the top bar to read it: calls to arms and peace offers to answer come first, then every news item of past weeks, newest first under a heading per day, with a switch between everything and only your realm. Each line with a place has a map button that takes you there. The button counts what came about your realm since you last looked, and blinks while a call or offer waits. When one of your battles or sieges begins, or a call to arms or peace offer arrives, a short alert drops in under the top bar with Go there (or Answer); it goes away on its own, and the log keeps what it said. A battle of yours also makes the week wait: tap Watch on its alert and the map goes there, the week plays on slowly enough to follow, and a strip along the bottom shows each side's men left against what they started with and the round; when the battle ends the strip says how. Tap End turn instead to play on without watching. 6. The Attention list and badge refresh, and the next orders phase begins. If the app goes to the background while one of your battles runs, it comes back to the same battle at the same step. If the app was killed, the last save and the written-down orders replay the month to that battle with the same result. The Needs attention screen The one list of warnings and of things waiting for you, titled "Needs attention". It opens from the bell, the badge, the controller's "next" button and the End turn question, as a card over the map. Group Examples Warnings Famine in a province within two months, pay owed to an army, an army hungry, a castle breached, a rising brewing, peace voices passing half against you, a ruler without an heir Waiting for you Events not yet answered, peace offers, idle armies and fleets, empty research or school slots, unspent levies, chances worth a look ("A lord across the border may be won over") and New entries for a system you meet for the first time Lines are listed most urgent first. Each has an icon, one sentence and a Show button that jumps to its place on the map or its card; Back returns to the Attention screen. Each line has two mute buttons: "Mute this" for that line and "Don't list this kind again" for every line of its kind. A long press opens the line's explanation with the same two buttons. Muted kinds are listed at the bottom and can be unmuted, and your mutes are kept in the save. The screen says what is wrong, never what to do. Its warnings and thresholds live in one config table to which each system adds its own lines. If Settings turns on the End turn confirmation, it names the count ("3 warnings wait for you · Look · End turn anyway"). Warnings never block the turn. Unanswered events are never in that question, because they always block End turn until you answer them. Other screens in a campaign - Battle view: while your battles run, Back takes you to the map and the battles keep running; the switcher brings you back. In a replay, Back returns to where the replay was opened. With a controller: A is pause and play, then Carry on; B goes back to the map (or leaves a replay); X is Retreat; Y shows the commander's line; the bumpers switch battle; Menu does nothing. - Siege view: a full screen opened from a besieged castle at local zoom or from its card; Back returns to the map at the castle. - Peace table: a modal opened from the Diplomacy section, an enemy's country card or an incoming offer, returning where it was opened. An incoming offer cannot be dismissed, only answered or put off one turn. - Map mode picker: a small pop-over from the tool column. - Confirmation: a small modal for destructive actions only, returning to the screen below unchanged. How a campaign ends Game over. When your realm no longer exists (annexed, or every province lost), the map zooms out over the old borders while the game over music plays, and a card says how it ended in one line with the date ("Burgundy was divided between France and the Empire · 1477") and your realm's highs: largest size, years lasted, battles won. It offers Look back (the News, read only), Play on as another realm (any realm on the current map) and Main menu. Play on is allowed in every campaign, ironman included, but it ends achievements for that campaign, says so on the button before you press it ("Achievements end for this campaign"), and cannot be undone. Winning. There are two ways to win. - World domination: you own, or hold as subjects, at least half of the world's settled land provinces. It is checked every January, and reaching it wins at once: the campaign end sequence plays straight away, and the final result offers Keep playing, which takes you back to the map until the end date. - Best at the end: when the end date comes, the realm that leads the Economy, Power or Technology score wins in that score. No margin is needed, and a tie shares the win. The scores are worked out every January for the Realm book; see Your realm. Campaign end. When the end date is reached (31 August 1939 by default, or the date chosen at the start) or you win by world domination, the final wrap-up events appear as normal event cards, then a closing sequence steps through your borders era by era at world zoom with the campaign end music, then the final result. There is no playing on past the end date. Final result. The scores of your realm and the five leading realms, the outcome (your wins, or with none your place in each score, such as "No victory · Economy 2nd · Power 3rd · Technology 2nd"), the achievements earned in this campaign, and Main menu or Credits. Achievements are earned only in ironman campaigns, so outside ironman the screen says so instead of showing an empty list. In the game today. The ending is one card over the map, the end card. It opens by itself when the end date comes, when your realm holds no land any more, or when the January turn finds your world domination, and the clock stops. It says how the campaign ended with the date ("France was divided between England and Burgundy · 1420", "The campaign ends · 31 August 1939", "World domination · 1700"), the outcome line, your score breakdown, the leading realms and your highs. After the end date it offers Look at the map (the End turn button becomes a crown that opens the card again) and New game ; after game over Play on as another realm (tap a realm, then Rule it; achievements end) and New game ; after world domination Keep playing and New game . The wrap-up events, the closing sequence, Look back and Credits come later. Interruptions - Going to the background (home button, a call, the screen locks) writes down your orders if you gave any since the last save, and suspends sound. - Coming back while still in memory, or a Steam Deck resuming from suspend, returns to the exact screen, scroll and camera without the title, with the load-and-resume music. - Killed in the background: the next start is a cold start with Continue pointing at that save, and after loading the map shows "Picked up where you left off". - A running turn pauses with the app and carries on when it returns; if the app was killed, the last save and the written-down orders are used. - Purchases: when the unlock flow ends it returns to where it was opened (the realm picker with the bought realm chosen, or the menu). A failed or cancelled purchase returns to the same place with no extra message beyond the store's. With no connection it says "No connection: try again later" and blocks nothing else. - Failure screen: when something fails that the game cannot recover from (the engine crashes, a save will not read), one screen says what failed in plain words and offers Restore the last save, Main menu and, where a crash reporter is approved, Send a report. Never a stack trace. Navigation by input Back on each device. Android: the system back button or gesture. iOS: the on-screen Back or ✕, with an edge swipe on full screens only, never over the map. Keyboard: Esc. Back on the map with nothing open opens the game menu; on the start screen it leaves the app on Android and does nothing elsewhere. Touch on the map. Tap selects a province, army or castle and shows its name tab; drag pans; pinch zooms; long press shows what is under your finger without selecting it. Tapping an army and then a province gives a march order at once, with no confirm step; tapping the army's own province halts it. Touch on cards, the book and menus. Tap presses; drag scrolls; pinch does nothing; long press shows the item's explanation (the same text as a desktop tooltip). Long press only explains; it never does anything you cannot also reach by tap. Where an explanation shows buttons, the same buttons are on the item itself. Controller. There are three sets of controls: Map on the map, Battle in the battle viewer, and Menu on every other screen (move focus, select, back, the bumpers to switch tabs or step through stacked cards, and Show on map). On the map: a free cursor on the left stick that snaps gently to provinces, armies and castles, pan on the right stick, zoom on the triggers, select, next army on the bumpers, and d-pad right for the Needs attention screen and its next line. A Steam Controller or Steam Deck trackpad acts as a mouse on the map and shows the pointer; otherwise the stick cursor shows. Focus. While a controller or keyboard is in use, exactly one element has focus, drawn with the gold frame used for the chosen map mode. A mouse works like touch with hover added; hover shows what long press shows. A keyboard uses Esc for Back, Enter to select, Tab and arrows to move focus, and Space or Enter held for half a second for End turn (a short Enter selects). Settings: Settings let you shape how Pocket Hegemony looks, sounds and handles on your device, from interface scale and colour vision to controller buttons and battery use. They never change the rules, balance or the computer players: anything that would is a campaign rule, chosen when you start a new game. Most settings pick sensible defaults from the kind of device you play on, apply at once, and follow you between devices if you sign in. Where you find it Open Settings from the game menu (the three-line button at the top left of the map, or Esc ) or from the start screen. Sections are on the left and their rows on the right; in a tall window the sections come first. Each row says what it does under its name, a red dot marks a value you changed, and a long press on the name (or a right-click) puts it back. Reset this section is at the end of each section. What the game has built so far: - Gameplay : Tutorial hints (with how many of the six are done) and Reset tutorial and hints; Achievement toasts; Autosave and Autosaves kept per campaign; Turn playback speed (1×, 2×, 4×: how fast the week plays out after End turn) and Battle playback speed. - Graphics : Battery saver (Off, Auto, On) and the knobs it moves: Frame rate cap, Sharpness and Animations. Rows it moves say "Set by Battery saver". Auto follows your device's battery where the browser reports it. - Audio : Master, Music on or off and its volume, Effects volume and Interface sounds. The speaker button's Sound card changes the same settings. - Accessibility : Text size (Normal, Large, Larger) for the cards, menus and alerts. Other rows join the screen as the game builds what they do. How it works The principles - Data, not code. Every setting is one entry in settings.yaml , with its section, type, options, default per device profile, platforms and how it applies. Adding or moving a setting, or changing a default, needs no code change, and the Settings screen is built from that file in its order. - A profile gives every default. On first launch the game picks a device profile and takes every default from it. - Changes apply at once. A change applies immediately with a preview behind the open panel; there is no Apply button. The only exception is Display mode, which asks "Keep this display?" and reverts after 15 seconds. - Every input works. Every row works with touch, mouse, keyboard and controller. No slider needs a drag and no row needs hover: sliders step with the d-pad or arrow keys and accept a tap at a position. - Nothing lost. Opening Settings in a campaign loses nothing, and closing it returns you to the exact map spot. - Never the simulation. Settings never change rules, balance or AI. Where Settings opens Settings opens as an overlay, from the cog on the title screen and from More. In a campaign, the game menu opens Settings over the dimmed map; Settings holds Campaign rules as a read-only section listing the rules the campaign started with. There is no separate pause menu. Esc or the Menu button opens the game menu. On Steam, the Controller section has a button that opens Steam's own binding panel. There is no settings wizard. On first launch, only these questions appear, and only when needed, each on one screen: the language (only when the system language is not supported); crash reports and usage statistics (when the privacy design requires consent); and "Is this text easy to read?" with Smaller, Fine and Bigger (Big screen profile only). The Settings screen In a landscape window (on every device) the section list is on the left, the section's rows on the right, and a one-line description of the focused row at the bottom. In a tall window (tablets in portrait, tall desktop windows) the section list comes first and a section's rows open full screen on tap, with Back to return. Phones are landscape only. The nine sections, in order: Gameplay, Graphics, Audio, Controls, Accessibility, Language, Account and cloud saves, Privacy, About. Each row shows its name, its current value, and a small "changed" dot when the value differs from the profile default. A long press on a row only explains it; right-click or X on a row resets it to its profile default. Each section ends with Reset this section, and About has Reset all settings. With a controller: LB and RB switch sections, the d-pad moves between rows, A changes or opens, d-pad left and right step a value, B goes back, X resets the row, and Y shows the long description. Connecting a controller on any profile adds controller prompts and focus outlines without switching profile. Auto interface scale picks the largest step at which a 360 × 640 CSS px layout still fits (small phones 100 %, large ones up to 125 %). Storage and sync Every setting belongs to one of two groups: Group What is in it Synced? Device Graphics, audio volumes, screen margins, controller deadzones, battery saver No, stays on this device Personal Gameplay, accessibility, language, key bindings, hint switches Yes, across your devices They live in two small JSON files, settings-device.json and settings-personal.json , each with a version number. While you are signed in to a Pocket Hegemony account, the personal file syncs through the account on every platform and across stores, the newest change winning setting by setting. Without an account, each store's free backup carries them: Steam Auto-Cloud on the personal file next to the save folder; iOS device backup and Android Auto Backup restore both files on a new device (no live sync); nothing on the web. The files are kept in the app's user data folder on desktop and Steam, in the mobile app's preferences on iOS and Android, and in localStorage on the web. On reading, unknown keys are dropped, invalid values fall back to the profile default, and a broken file never stops the game from starting. When a file's version goes up, small migration steps rename or convert keys. Settings are never stored inside a campaign save, so loading any save never changes anyone's settings. Moving from the free tier to the full game keeps your settings. Campaign rules These are chosen on the new game screen, saved in the campaign, and shown read-only in Settings, under Campaign rules: - difficulty; - AI temper; - fog of war; - historical or free events; - ironman (achievements only count in ironman); - the campaign end date (default 31 August 1939); - whether music eras follow the calendar or technology. The map mode menu's "Hide unexplored lands" stays a display switch, because it only hides unknown lands visually. It would become a campaign rule only if fog ever hid information the computer uses. Language - Language: the launch list; default is the system language if supported, otherwise English. Interface text changes live; event and catalogue text reload on the next panel open. A language in a non-Latin script joins the list only once the localisation design has a font for it, because the pixel font covers Latin only. - Number format: follows the language, 1,000.5, 1.000,5 or 1 000,5. Account, privacy and about - Account: Sign in or Create account; when signed in, your email and Sign out. Default signed out, never a wall before playing. The Load screen's "Sign in to sync" opens the same flow. - While signed in: Cloud saves (On by default, syncing saves and personal settings), Sync on Wi-Fi only (Off by default), the list of signed-in devices each with Sign out, and Delete account and saves with a confirmation (also reachable from Privacy). - Privacy: Send crash reports and Send anonymous usage statistics (asked on first launch), and, in the free mobile tier only if the ad stays, Ad consent, which reopens the consent form. - About: version and build number, Restore purchases (which Apple requires to be reachable), Credits and licences, Reset all settings, and Copy diagnostics (the diagnostics line and your settings on the clipboard for support). Platform notes - Steam Deck: body text about 19 px at 112 % (17 px at 100 %) at 1280 × 800; starts fullscreen with Deck glyphs; Settings needs no mouse or keyboard anywhere; naming a save calls Steam's floating gamepad keyboard. - Big screen: 175 % scale and Large text (the same physical size at 4K), a slow cursor, a 5 % margin with the calibration screen, focus outlines always on. - Safe areas (notch, home bar, camera hole) are always respected; this is not a setting. - Android: the back gesture behaves like B or Esc : it closes the top panel, then opens the game menu, and never quits the game from the map without asking. - iOS: the silent switch and "Let other apps' audio play" use the native ambient audio session. The settings file format Each entry in settings.yaml carries an id ( section.name , also the key in the settings files), section , type (choice, toggle, slider, binding, action), options , default , default by profile , platforms , hide on (rows Steam Input owns), applies (live, view, restart), sync (device or personal) and optionally sets when on . A slider adds min , max and step ; an action is a button such as Reset or Restore purchases. Names and descriptions are string keys ( settings.<id .name , settings.<id .desc ), never text in the file. Tests - A smoke test opens Settings on each profile, steps through every row with the keyboard only, and fails if focus is lost or a row cannot be reached. - A schema test checks that settings.yaml loads, every default is one of its options, and every string key exists in English. - The accessibility checks include screenshots of the map in each colour vision mode run through a colour-blindness simulator. - On a Steam Deck, every row must be reachable with the built-in controls and legible at arm's length. What you see The Settings screen with its nine sections, the changed dot, per-row and per-section reset, the "Keep this display?" question, the calibration screen, "Set by …" on driven rows, and the read-only Campaign rules section. How it connects - Saving: the autosave values, the Cloud saves row, Wi-Fi only, account and devices; personal settings ride the same account sync and store backups. - Screens and navigation: where Settings opens, Confirm End turn, the turn report, the Far layout, scale and text size, prompts, hold actions, main hand, Android back. - Music and sound: buses, volumes, music variety, zoom mix, ambience, haptics, captions, reduced intensity, mono and background play. - Map and Map Modes: sharpness, map detail, animations, frame cap, colour vision, borders, patterns, place names and the parchment switch. - Tutorial and help: tutorial hints and their reset, tooltips and their delay, detailed tooltips. - Achievements: the toast switch; achievements only count in ironman. - The 1378 start: the campaign rules shown read-only. - How a turn works: Keep screen awake during the computer players' turn. - Warfare: battle playback speed and battle view controls. - Historical events: Jump to events.
